userStories.title: Add granular RBAC permission checks to all CRUD and sensitive endpoints

Bulk operation endpoints (/api/*/bulk-update, /api/*/bulk-delete) require elevated permissions (scope: _all or _team)

Document the complete permission matrix: endpoint → required permissions in a permissions-matrix.ts file
Add tests verifying permission denial returns 403 with descriptive message

userStories.notes: Many endpoints currently only check requireAuth (is the user logged in?) but not requirePermission (does the user have the right role/permission?). Bulk operations and DELETE routes are the highest risk. The enhanced-rbac-middleware.ts has full support for granular permissions but adoption is incomplete.

userStories.title: Implement optimistic mutations for inline edits and status changes

Apply to inline cell edits in table views (status changes, field updates)
Apply to drag-and-drop stage changes on pipeline boards
Apply to toggle operations (active/inactive, pin/unpin, archive/unarchive)

userStories.notes: Currently pages use queryClient.invalidateQueries() which does a full refetch after every mutation. userStories.title: Enforce role-based route protection for all unguarded CRM, admin, and finance pages
userStories.description: As a platform owner, I need every page in the application to enforce minimum role permissions so that sales reps cannot access admin functions, company admins cannot reach root/platform admin pages, and finance pages are restricted to finance roles, preventing unauthorized access through direct URL navigation.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit all routes in client/src/App.tsx and identify every Route that renders a component directly without ProtectedRoute wrapping

Apply ProtectedRoute to all CRM routes (/crm/deals, /crm/leads, /crm/contacts, /crm/companies, /leads, /customers, /deals, /opportunities) with permissions: ['sales.lead.view_own', 'sales.lead.view_team', 'sales.customer.view_own']
Apply ProtectedRoute to sales management routes (/quotes, /quotes/new, /quotes/:id, /proposal-builder, /quote-proposal-generation) with permissions: ['sales.quote.view_own', 'sales.quote.view_team']
Apply ProtectedRoute to finance routes (/advanced-billing, /commission-management) with permissions: ['finance.billing.view', 'finance.reports.view'] and minLevel: 3
Apply ProtectedRoute to operations routes (/purchase-orders, /warehouse-operations, /equipment-lifecycle, /product-hub) with permissions: ['operations.inventory.view', 'service.equipment.view']
Apply ProtectedRoute to analytics/reporting routes (/sales-performance-analytics, /sales-command-center, /service-analytics) with permissions: ['reporting.sales.view'] and minLevel: 3
Routes using AdminRouteGuard (minLevel 7) must remain on: /admin-command-center, /root-admin-signups-crm, /root-admin/seo and all /admin/* paths
Routes using platformOnly must remain on: /admin-hub, /root-admin-dashboard, /admin/tenant-management, /admin/platform-analytics, /admin/database-management, /admin/mobile-logs, /admin/audit-logs
All routes that previously had no guard must now show the AccessDenied component for users without the required permissions — NOT a blank page or 404
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: CRITICAL security story. Current App.tsx audit shows most routes at /crm/*, /quotes/*, /customers, /leads, /purchase-orders, /warehouse-operations, /commission-management, and /sales-command-center render components directly with no ProtectedRoute wrapper. A sales rep can navigate directly to /advanced-billing or /commission-management via URL. The RouteGuard and ProtectedRoute components already exist in client/src/components/auth/ — this story is purely applying them consistently. Reference: client/src/components/auth/ProtectedRoute.tsx and client/src/lib/navigation-permissions.ts for the permission map.

userStories.title: Build role-aware sidebar navigation that hides sections users cannot access

alwaysVisible sections (dashboard, tasks, ai-hub, knowledge-base, settings, crm) remain visible to all authenticated users

Add a hook useVisibleNavItems() in client/src/hooks/ that returns the filtered navigation tree using navigation-permissions.ts rules

Typecheck passes: npm run check

The sidebar component is at client/src/components/layout/ — identify the correct file and apply the filter there.

userStories.title: Implement role-scoped API data filtering so reps only see their own records
userStories.description: As a sales manager, I need records to be automatically scoped to what each user is authorized to see at the API level — reps see only their own leads and quotes, managers see their team's, directors see their region's — so data isolation is enforced on the server, not just the UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Review server/middleware/hierarchical-query-builder.ts — ensure buildScopedQuery() is applied to all GET list endpoints for: /api/leads, /api/customers, /api/proposals, /api/deals-management/deals, /api/contacts

Scope tiers must map to role levels: roleLevel 1-2 (own records: userId match), roleLevel 3-4 (team records: teamId match), roleLevel 5-6 (regional records: regionId match), roleLevel 7+ (company-wide: tenantId only)
Platform admins (roleLevel 8, isPlatformAdmin=true) bypass all scoping and see all tenants
Each scoped endpoint must read the user's roleLevel, teamId, regionId from the JWT/session via getUserId() and getTenantId() helpers
Create a server/middleware/scope-middleware.ts helper: applyScopeFilter(req, baseQuery, table) that injects the correct WHERE clause based on role
Scoped endpoints return only records the user is authorized to see — a rep calling GET /api/leads must not receive another rep's leads
Add integration test in server/tests/integration/ verifying scope isolation: rep A cannot see rep B's leads, manager sees both, director sees all in region
Existing admin-level endpoints that intentionally return all records (platform admin routes) must document this explicitly with a comment
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: hierarchical-query-builder.ts exists at server/middleware/hierarchical-query-builder.ts but is not applied consistently across all list endpoints. Currently most endpoints only filter by tenantId which means any authenticated user in the tenant sees all records. This is correct for admins but wrong for reps. The enhanced-rbac-middleware.ts provides EnhancedUserContext with roleLevel, teamId, regionId, territoryScope — use these for scoping. This is a data security story, not just UI.

userStories.title: Add role-specific dashboard views that surface relevant KPIs and actions per role
userStories.description: As a sales rep, when I log in I should see a dashboard focused on my leads, my quotes, and my tasks — not company-wide revenue charts. As a manager, I should see my team's pipeline. As an executive, I see company-wide KPIs. The dashboard should present the right information for each role automatically.
acceptanceCriteria: Modify the main Dashboard page (client/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx or equivalent) to detect the user's roleLevel from usePermissions() and render the appropriate view
roleLevel 1-2 (Individual Contributor / Team Lead): Show 'My Pipeline' widgets — My Open Leads count, My Active Quotes with total value, My Upcoming Tasks (next 7 days), My Recent Activity feed
roleLevel 3-4 (Supervisor / Manager): Show team widgets — Team Pipeline Summary by stage, Team Quota Attainment %, Top Performing Reps (ranked by deals closed this month), Team Activity Feed
roleLevel 5-6 (Regional / Company Director): Show regional widgets — Regional Revenue vs Target, Pipeline by Stage (all teams in region), Deals at Risk (no activity > 14 days), Conversion Rate trend
roleLevel 7-8 (Executive / Platform Admin): Show company-wide KPIs — Total Revenue MTD/YTD, MRR, NRR, Customer Count, ARR Forecast, Churn Rate
Each dashboard tier must use the existing KpiSummaryBar component with role-appropriate metrics
Quick action buttons on each tier: Rep → 'New Lead', 'New Quote'; Manager → 'Review Pipeline', 'Team Assignments'; Director → 'Reports', 'Forecast'; Admin → 'Admin Hub', 'System Settings'
Dashboard does not redirect or change URL — same route / but renders different components based on role
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Currently the Dashboard at / renders a single view for all roles. KpiSummaryBar component exists at client/src/components/dashboard/KpiSummaryBar.tsx and accepts configurable metrics. This is a high-impact UX improvement — reps currently see company-wide charts that aren't actionable for them. usePermissions() returns level and role tier. The API scoping from RBAC-003 means the data returned is already role-scoped, so the dashboard widgets can use the same endpoints and get role-appropriate data.

userStories.title: Implement contextual 'Quick Actions' button strip on all entity detail pages

acceptanceCriteria: Create a reusable QuickActionsBar component in client/src/components/ui/quick-actions-bar.tsx that accepts: entityType, entityId, currentStatus, and an actions array
Actions are state-aware: the available actions change based on the record's current status field

Lead quick actions by status: New → ['Qualify', 'Schedule Call', 'Create Quote', 'Disqualify']; Contacted → ['Log Call', 'Create Quote', 'Schedule Follow-up']; Qualified → ['Create Quote', 'Convert to Customer']; Won → ['Create Quote', 'View Customer']; Lost → ['Reopen', 'Archive']
Customer quick actions: ['New Quote', 'Log Activity', 'Schedule Service', 'Create Invoice', 'Add Contact']

Integrate QuickActionsBar into CustomerDetail.tsx at the top of the page, below the header
Integrate QuickActionsBar into the lead and deal detail pages

userStories.notes: Currently all actions on detail pages are in dropdown kebab menus or tab-buried buttons. HubSpot puts primary actions (Email, Call, Create Note, Schedule Meeting) directly in the header. This story solves the 'buried actions' problem. The navigation with query params is the precursor to QP-001 (auto-populating quotes from customer context). Each action button should respect RBAC — if the user lacks sales.quote.create_own permission, hide the 'New Quote' button rather than show an error after clicking.

userStories.title: Build a streamlined inline edit mode for record detail fields to reduce edit-page navigation
userStories.description: As a sales rep, I should be able to click any field on a customer or lead detail page to edit it inline and save without navigating to a separate edit form, matching how modern CRMs allow fast field updates during a call or meeting.
acceptanceCriteria: Create an InlineEditField component in client/src/components/ui/inline-edit-field.tsx supporting field types: text, textarea, select, date, phone, email, currency, number
Clicking a field value on a detail page replaces it with an input in edit mode; pressing Enter or clicking outside saves; pressing Escape cancels
On save, fire a PATCH /api/:entityType/:id request with only the changed field (partial update)

Apply InlineEditField to CustomerDetail.tsx for fields: companyName, phone, email, website, address, industry, accountStatus, assignedUserId
Apply InlineEditField to lead detail pages for fields: firstName, lastName, email, phone, company, status, source, assignedUserId

assignedUserId field uses a searchable user select dropdown populated from GET /api/users?tenantId=xxx
Changes made via inline edit must invalidate the relevant TanStack Query cache key so other components on the page reflect the update

userStories.notes: Currently CustomerDetail.tsx and lead detail pages require navigating to a separate edit form or opening a modal to change any field. This is a 3-click workflow that inline editing reduces to 1 click. PATCH endpoints already exist for customers and leads (server/routes-*.ts). The InlineEditField component pattern is common in CRMs — refer to HubSpot's click-to-edit behavior. TanStack Query invalidation: use queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['/api/customers', id] }) after a successful PATCH.

userStories.title: Add global keyboard shortcuts and command palette for power-user navigation

acceptanceCriteria: Implement a CommandPalette component in client/src/components/ui/command-palette.tsx using shadcn/ui Command (cmdk) component

Register the command palette at the App root level (App.tsx) so it works on all pages

userStories.notes: cmdk is already available via shadcn/ui Command component. This is a high-delight feature for sales reps who work at volume. The command palette should be lazy-loaded and not impact initial page load. Sequential key combos (N then L) are simpler to implement than chords and avoid conflicts with browser shortcuts. The RBAC filter is important — showing 'Go to Admin Hub' to a rep who cannot access it creates confusion.

userStories.title: Enable quote creation pre-seeded with customer and contact data from the record context
userStories.description: As a sales rep, when I click 'New Quote' from a customer or lead detail page, the quote builder should automatically fill in the company name, primary contact, billing address, and any existing equipment so I don't have to re-enter information I'm already looking at.
acceptanceCriteria: Modify the 'New Quote' navigation action on CustomerDetail.tsx to navigate to /quotes/new?businessRecordId={id}&companyName={encodeURIComponent(name)}&contactId={primaryContactId}&contactName={encodeURIComponent(contactName)}
Modify QuoteBuilderPage.tsx to read URL search params (businessRecordId, companyName, contactId, contactName) on mount using useSearch() from wouter

userStories.notes: Currently /quotes/new opens a blank QuoteBuilderPage. The customer, contact, and company fields must be filled manually even when navigating from a customer record. userStories.title: Build a multi-step quote wizard with progress indicator to reduce quote creation errors
userStories.description: As a sales rep, I need the quote creation flow to guide me through clearly labeled steps (Customer, Products, Pricing, Review & Send) with a visible progress indicator so I know what's required at each step and don't accidentally skip required fields before sending.
acceptanceCriteria: Refactor QuoteBuilderPage.tsx into a multi-step wizard with 4 steps: Step 1 'Customer & Contact' (skip if pre-seeded from QP-001), Step 2 'Products & Line Items', Step 3 'Pricing & Terms', Step 4 'Review & Send'
Add a horizontal step progress indicator at the top of the wizard showing all 4 steps with the current step highlighted and completed steps marked with a checkmark
Step 1 (Customer & Contact): company name (required), primary contact (required), billing address, quote expiry date (default: 30 days from today)

userStories.notes: Current QuoteBuilderPage is a single-form page. Converting to a wizard reduces cognitive load and prevents incomplete quotes from being sent. The Review step in Step 4 can reuse the existing QuoteView component in read-only mode. Pre-seeding from QP-001 means Step 1 is skipped — implement by tracking a completedSteps Set and marking step 1 complete if businessRecordId param was present.

acceptanceCriteria: Create server/scripts/sql-injection-audit.ts that statically scans all route files for raw SQL string concatenation, template literals in db.execute(), and sql.raw() without parameterization

Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Some pages like Contacts.tsx and Invoices.tsx reference undo patterns but implementation is inconsistent. A standardized hook ensures all destructive actions follow the same undo pattern. This significantly reduces user anxiety around delete operations.

userStories.title: Fix critical SQL injection in storage.ts getBusinessRecords via string interpolation
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I need the SQL injection vulnerability in storage.ts getBusinessRecords() fixed because user-controlled parameters (recordType, status, search, limit) are directly interpolated into raw SQL strings via template literals and sql.raw(), allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary SQL.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace string interpolation in WHERE clause construction (lines 2733-2746) with Drizzle ORM parameterized queries
Replace sql.raw(whereClause) with proper Drizzle where() conditions using eq(), like(), and(), or()
Replace sql.raw(limitClause) with Drizzle .limit() method
All parameters (tenantId, recordType, status, search, limit) use parameterized queries only
Search functionality uses parameterized LIKE with sql`...${searchTerm}...` not string interpolation
No sql.raw() calls remain in getBusinessRecords()
Existing business records functionality works identically
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: FIXED: Replaced all string interpolation and sql.raw() in getBusinessRecords() with Drizzle ORM parameterized queries using eq(), or(), sql template literals with parameter binding, and .limit(). Added bounds checking on limit parameter (capped at 500). No sql.raw() calls remain in the method.

userStories.title: Fix critical SQL injection in routes-custom-reports.ts via sql.raw(filter.value)
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I need the SQL injection vulnerability in routes-custom-reports.ts fixed because filter.value from request body is passed directly to sql.raw() inside an INTERVAL clause, allowing an attacker to break out of the interval and inject arbitrary SQL.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace sql.raw(filter.value) on line 782 with a validated and parameterized numeric value
Validate that filter.value is a positive integer before use in the INTERVAL clause
Use Drizzle parameterized query: sql`interval '1 day' * ${validatedDays}` or equivalent safe pattern
Reject non-numeric filter.value with appropriate error response
Custom reports last_n_days filter works identically for valid numeric inputs
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: FIXED: Replaced sql.raw(filter.value) with parseInt() validation and parameterized interval multiplication: sql`${column} >= CURRENT_DATE - (${days} * interval '1 day')`. Validates days is a positive integer between 0 and 3650. Returns null (no filter) for invalid values.

userStories.description: Architectural fix: server/middleware/edge-function-proxy.ts currently does JSON.stringify(req.body) which corrupts multipart/form-data uploads (CSV imports), and uses await response.text() which corrupts binary responses (PDFs, ZIP downloads). acceptanceCriteria: Detect Content-Type on the incoming request: if multipart/form-data, stream the raw body with the boundary preserved (use Express's raw body buffer if available, or pipe the request)
Detect Content-Type on the edge response: if not JSON-ish (text/*, application/json), use response.arrayBuffer() and res.end(Buffer.from(buf)) to preserve binary

Add unit test for binary response (mock edge function returning a PNG, verify byte-equal pass-through)

userStories.notes: DONE 2026-05-04. userStories.title: Audit and fix pathParts indexing across edge functions
userStories.completionNotes: PARTIAL DONE 2026-05-05. Audit confirmed supabase/functions/server.ts:108 strips the function name in production (Coolify deployment via Dockerfile.edge-functions). 30+ edge functions index pathParts[1] for the resource ID, expecting the function name to still be at [0] — so all their /:id and /:id/<action> routes return 404 in production. Created supabase/functions/_shared/path.ts with normalizePath(pathname, functionName) helper that tolerates BOTH calling conventions (post-strip + prefix-preserved); 15 unit tests in server/tests/unit/edge-shared-path.test.ts cover boundary cases. Migrated the 7 EDGE-002 SAFE domains that are in active proxy production use: notifications, cross-module, roles, territories, vendors, webhooks, knowledge-base (consolidated its in-file engagementPath into the shared helper). The remaining ~23 broken functions (activities, admin, automation, billing, contracts, contract-renewal, customer-portal, customer-segments, dashboards, equipment, file-storage, fleet, invoices, monitoring-clients, platform-crm, printer-monitoring, purchase-orders, quickbooks, renewal-activities, renewal-playbooks, role-management, sales-territories, service-contracts, service-tickets, subscriptions, technician-management, templates, user-management, work-orders, workflows) have the same bug but aren't in proxy production use yet — tracked as EDGE-002m-remainder. tsc errors unchanged (9984). 48 tests pass. npm run build: ✓ 1m 34s.
userStories.description: supabase/functions/server.ts:108 strips the function name from the URL before dispatching to the handler (newUrl.pathname = '/' + pathParts.slice(1).join('/')). Many edge function dispatchers index pathParts[1] for the resource ID, assuming the function name is still in the URL. Under server.ts they index off-by-one and resource routes never fire. This is a pre-existing bug but worth surfacing now.
acceptanceCriteria: Inventory edge functions that index pathParts[1] without first stripping their own function-name prefix
Decide on a canonical helper: a _shared/path.ts that returns normalized pathParts regardless of caller (server.ts strips, Supabase native runtime doesn't)
Refactor each affected function to use the helper, OR update server.ts to NOT strip (and fix functions that assume strip)
Add a smoke test to /supabase/functions/_test that hits both modes
Verify activities/:id, notifications/:id, etc. work after fix
userStories.notes: Foundational fix landed for the 7 EDGE-002 SAFE domains that are in proxy production use. See EDGE-002m-remainder for the other ~23 functions.

userStories.title: Canon abook.csv parser with Crypto v2 password decryption
userStories.description: As a help desk user, I want to upload a Canon abook.csv and have its entries decoded into canonical form, with my source password used to decrypt SMB credentials.
acceptanceCriteria: New file supabase/functions/_shared/address-book/canon/parser.ts exports parseCanon(buffer, password?) → ParseResult
Reads header comments: # Canon AddressBook CSV version, # CharSet, # Crypto Version, # Crypto Attribute, # SubAddressBookName
Maps objectclass=email rows to canonical email entries (display_name from cn, email from mailaddress, speed_dial_index from indxid)
Maps objectclass=remotefilesystem rows with protocol=smb to canonical smb entries (smb_full_unc from url, smb_share_path from path, smb_username from username)

When '# Crypto Attribute: pwd' is set, decrypts the pwd column using user-supplied password via Canon Crypto v2 KDF (PBKDF2 → AES-256-CBC); algorithm verified against the supplied sample with password '1' and the blob qXiioxBKG3fl7dAwodxTOw==
Stores all 49 source columns in source_metadata for round-trip fidelity
Returns parse errors per row without aborting the whole file
Unit test loads tests/fixtures/address-book/canon-sample.csv (copy of repo-root abook.csv) with password '1' and asserts row count plus a known SMB credential decrypts to a non-empty string
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Source PRD: US-004. Sample file exists at repo root: abook.csv. Risk: Canon Crypto v2 KDF specifics (iteration count, salt source) are not publicly documented; if reverse-engineering exceeds time budget, document the exact failure and fall back to ABK-004-FALLBACK (parser produces entries with credential_id=null and reports them in errors_json).

userStories.title: Canon abook.csv serializer with optional password re-encryption
userStories.description: As a help desk user, I want to export a canonical address book back to Canon abook.csv format so it can be re-imported on a Canon device.
acceptanceCriteria: New file supabase/functions/_shared/address-book/canon/serializer.ts exports serializeCanon(book, entries, options) → SerializeResult
Output begins with the Canon header comments using the configured CSV version, charset, and SubAddressBookName

Implemented: blog-post-revisions edge function (list/get/create/restore with dedup + audit), 10s autosave from BlogPostEditor (revision_source='manual'), BlogPostHistory page with diffLines from npm 'diff' package + restore alert dialog, retention via blog_agent_settings.revision_retention_days (default 90, range 7-730) and POST /blog-post-revisions/cleanup which preserves the latest revision per post.

userStories.title: Asset library: images, quotes, data, expert contacts
userStories.description: As an editor, I want a single place to manage reusable assets so research and visuals are findable across posts.
acceptanceCriteria: Assets table with type enum: image, quote, data_table, expert_contact, link, file
Upload to S3-compatible storage (Cloudflare R2 / Supabase Storage adapter)
Image assets: auto-generate thumbnails, extract EXIF, store dimensions, original filename, alt text, license/source
Quote assets: text, attributed_to, source_url, retrieved_at, license
Data table assets: csv upload → preview, column types, optional chart preview
Expert contact assets: name, expertise tags, email/contact, prior quotes given, response rate
Search across assets by tag, type, text
userStories.notes: License/source on every asset is non-negotiable for E-E-A-T and legal safety. Implemented: Supabase Storage bucket 'blog-assets' (25 MB cap, image+csv+pdf+json+text mime allowlist) provisioned via _backfill_blog_assets_bucket.sql. blog-assets edge function with list/get/create/patch/delete + POST /upload-url that issues a signed upload URL to a tenant-scoped path '<tenant_id>/<uuid>-<filename>' (refuses cross-tenant storage paths on create). Library page at /platform-admin/blog/assets with type filter, free-text search across title/description/attribution, type-colored card grid, soft delete with confirm. Upload modal with type-specific forms (image: alt text required; quote: text + attribution/source URL; expert_contact: name/title/org/contact/expertise tags). Image picker dialog integrated into BlogEditor — replaces the prior window.prompt flow on both the toolbar Image button and the slash-menu Image entry; supports inline 'upload new' and auto-selects the freshly uploaded asset. Deferred: thumbnail generation, EXIF extraction, CSV preview/column-typing, expert-contact response-rate tracking, link asset type — each a follow-up since each is its own non-trivial pipeline. Schema's enum is {image, quote, data, expert_contact, file}; AC's 'data_table' and 'link' types not added to enum since (a) 'data' covers data tables and (b) link assets are already representable as URLs in body markdown without their own row.

userStories.title: Audit log for every mutating action
userStories.description: As a workspace owner, I want a tamper-evident audit log so I can investigate incidents and prove compliance.
acceptanceCriteria: audit_log table: workspace_id, actor_user_id, action (string), target_type, target_id, before (jsonb), after (jsonb), ip, user_agent, created_at
Middleware logs every POST/PATCH/DELETE on the API
Admin UI: audit log viewer with filters (actor, action, date range)
Logs retained 1 year minimum; configurable
Append-only — no UPDATE or DELETE permission on audit_log via RLS
userStories.notes: Consider periodic export to immutable storage (S3 with object lock) for tamper-evidence.

userStories.title: Background job queue with retries and observability
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a reliable job system so AI calls, syndication, and analytics ingest can run async with backoff.
acceptanceCriteria: pg-boss (preferred — uses Postgres) or BullMQ adapter
Job types defined as TypeScript discriminated unions; handlers in apps/worker
Default policy: exponential backoff (1m, 5m, 30m, 2h), max 5 attempts
Job dashboard in admin UI: pending, active, failed, completed counts; retry / cancel buttons
Failed jobs surface in audit_log with full error stack
Idempotency keys on every job to prevent duplicate work
userStories.notes: pg-boss avoids a Redis dependency for small deployments. Implemented as a lightweight Postgres-native queue (no pg-boss/BullMQ since the deploy has no always-on Node worker — everything is Deno edge functions). Built: blog_jobs table (status/priority/scheduled_at/attempts/max_attempts/last_error/result/idempotency_key/locked_until/locked_by), POST /blog-jobs (enqueue with idempotency dedup), GET /blog-jobs/stats (queued/active/failed/completed/cancelled counts), GET /blog-jobs?status&type, POST /blog-jobs/:id/retry, POST /blog-jobs/:id/cancel, POST /blog-jobs/run-due (cron entry point — claims due jobs with two-step UPDATE ... WHERE status='queued' AND id IN(...) approximating SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, runs in-process, applies 1m/5m/30m/2h exponential backoff, marks final fail after max_attempts). Built-in handlers: noop (smoke test) + retention_cleanup (invokes US-BLOG-009 cleanup logic). Dashboard at /platform-admin/blog/settings/jobs with status cards (5s polling), filterable jobs table, retry/cancel actions, expandable row showing payload/result/stack. Every state transition writes a blog_audit_log row (enqueue, complete, fail_retry, fail_permanent, retry, cancel). External cron wiring (k8s CronJob → POST /blog-jobs/run-due) is operations-side, not in this story.

userStories.title: Keyword research adapter interface + DataForSEO reference adapter
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want keyword data (volume, difficulty, CPC, trend) so I can prioritize topics with measurable demand.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/core/keyword-adapter.ts: searchVolume, keywordDifficulty, relatedKeywords, autocomplete, trend12mo
Adapters: dataforseo (reference), ahrefs, semrush, google-keyword-planner — all implementing the same interface
Workspace setting: which adapter + API credentials (encrypted)
Keyword cache table to avoid re-querying within TTL (default 30 days)
Bulk lookup endpoint: paste a list of seed keywords → returns enriched data
Cost tracking: every adapter call logs estimated cost in cents to ai_costs table
userStories.notes: Cost tracking matters — keyword APIs are metered and bills sneak up fast.

userStories.title: Search intent classifier
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want every keyword classified by intent so I plan the right content format.
acceptanceCriteria: Classifier tags each keyword: informational, commercial-investigation, transactional, navigational, with confidence score
Implementation: LLM prompt that takes keyword + top 10 SERP titles/snippets and returns intent + reasoning
Bulk classify on keyword import; cached on keywords.intent column
Admin UI: filter keyword list by intent; intent shown as colored chip
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-05-17. Shared classifier supabase/functions/_shared/blog/keyword/intent-classifier.ts (Claude, temp 0, JSON-only prompt, graceful degrade on parse failure, 0-100/0-1 confidence coercion, synonym tolerance). New edge function supabase/functions/blog-keywords/index.ts: GET / (intent/search/source_type/cluster_id/unclassified filters + paging + tenant-wide intent_counts), POST /classify (bulk; pulls top-10 organic titles+snippets from latest blog_serp_snapshots per keyword when use_serp, caches intent on blog_keywords.intent, stores confidence/reasoning/serp_informed/classified_at in raw_data.intent_meta, audit-logged), PATCH /:id manual override (audit-logged). Intent stored as 4 short canonical values (commercial = PRD commercial-investigation, varchar(20) safe). Frontend client/src/pages/platform-admin/blog/BlogKeywords.tsx: filterable table, colored intent chips, confidence %, SERP-informed dot, one-click Classify unclassified, per-row reclassify + manual-override select. Wired into App.tsx route /platform-admin/blog/keywords and BlogShell nav (g k). SCOPE: 'classify on keyword import' delivered as a bulk endpoint + one-click UI rather than an auto-trigger inside the PAA miner hot path (auto per-keyword LLM calls during a mine of hundreds of PAA rows would be cost/latency-prohibitive). No DB migration: reused existing raw_data jsonb. tsc clean for new files, vite build green (BlogKeywords lazy-chunked 6.86 kB).

userStories.title: SERP analyzer for any keyword
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want to see what currently ranks so I can match or exceed the bar.
acceptanceCriteria: SERP fetcher (DataForSEO or scraping adapter) returns top 20 organic results + SERP features (PAA, featured snippet, knowledge panel, video, image pack, local pack)
For each result: URL, title, meta description, domain, estimated DA, word count (fetched + parsed), heading structure (H2/H3)
Aggregated metrics: median word count, common headings, common entities, dominant content type (listicle/guide/comparison/etc.)
Stored in serp_snapshots table with fetched_at timestamp; re-fetch on demand or weekly
Admin UI: SERP analyzer view with sortable table + aggregate summary card
userStories.notes: Word count parsing must handle paywalls and JS-rendered content gracefully — fall back to meta description length when blocked. Implemented: KeywordAdapter contract extended with optional fetchSerp(creds, keyword, opts) returning {organic, features, cost}. DataForSEO impl wraps POST /v3/serp/google/organic/live/advanced and maps items to organic (rank/url/title/description/domain), featured_snippet, paa (with expanded answers), knowledge_panel, has_video_pack/image_pack/local_pack. blog_serp_snapshots table caches per (tenant, keyword, location_code, language_code, fetched_at). blog-serp edge function: POST /blog-serp/fetch (fetches, does best-effort per-URL parse with 3s timeout + 6 concurrency, falls back to snippet word-count when blocked), GET /blog-serp (list summaries), GET /blog-serp/:id (full), DELETE /blog-serp/:id. Aggregates computed at insert time: median/mean word count, common H2s (top 5, normalized + folded, requires count>=2), dominant_content_type heuristic (listicle/how_to/comparison/guide/review based on title patterns; nulls when no clear winner). Admin UI at /platform-admin/blog/serp with keyword + location + language input, recent snapshots sidebar, aggregate summary card, feature chips, sortable organic table (rank/word_count/domain), PAA section. New blog sub-nav entry 'SERP' (g e shortcut). Deferred: estimated DA (would need a separate DA lookup adapter — Moz / Ahrefs DR), common entities (NLP — could be heuristic noun-phrase extraction or LLM-driven later), automatic weekly re-fetch (will hook into US-BLOG-012 job queue once cron is wired).

userStories.title: People Also Ask + autocomplete miner
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want every related question surfaced so my content covers the actual user journey.
acceptanceCriteria: Recursive PAA crawler: fetch PAA for seed keyword, then for each PAA result, fetch its PAA (depth 2 default, configurable up to 4)
Google autocomplete fetcher: A-Z + 0-9 prefix expansion for seed keyword
Results stored in keywords table with source = 'paa' or 'autocomplete' and parent keyword reference
Deduplication and grouping by lexical similarity
Admin UI: tree view of PAA chains; click to add to brief
userStories.notes: Respect rate limits — back off aggressively on 429s. Implemented: extended blog_keywords with source_type, parent_keyword_id (self-FK), parent_question, mining_depth columns (backfill SQL idempotent). blog-paa-miner edge function: POST /mine (BFS over PAA up to depth 4, persists each Q with parent link; concurrent autocomplete fan-out across A-Z + 0-9 prefixes — 36 calls/seed when enabled; both passes share a normalized-keyword dedup set so the same string never round-trips twice), GET /tree?keyword= (walks descendants via parent_keyword_id, splits into PAA chain + flat autocomplete list, capped at 2000 nodes), DELETE /clear?keyword= (removes descendants only, preserves seed). Uses the existing tenant DataForSEO target. Adapter calls wrapped in retryOn429 (single 2-second pause). UI at /platform-admin/blog/paa with keyword + depth + location/language + toggles for PAA and autocomplete, expandable tree view (chevron toggles, ChildrenMap rendered recursively), copy-on-click + 'Copy all PAA' bulk export, autocomplete shown as wrap-friendly chip cloud, 'Clear run' destructive action. New blog sub-nav 'PAA' (g q shortcut). Dedup is exact normalized-string match (lowercase + alphanumeric); near-duplicate clustering by Levenshtein/Jaro deferred — current dedup is enough for v1 since DataForSEO normalizes most rephrasings.

userStories.title: Forum / community question miner (Reddit, Quora, Stack Exchange)
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want real questions from real users so my content addresses authentic pain rather than synthetic SEO phrases.
acceptanceCriteria: Reddit: search across configured subreddits via Reddit API; extract question titles + top comments
Quora: scrape (within ToS) or use Bright Data adapter for question + top answer snippets
Stack Exchange: API integration for relevant sites (StackOverflow, SuperUser, etc.)
Each question stored as a 'community_question' row with source, url, score/upvotes, captured_at
LLM clusters questions by theme; clusters surface in the brief generator
Configurable seed list per workspace (subreddits, Quora topics, SE sites)
userStories.notes: Always store source URL — citations from real questions strengthen E-E-A-T.

userStories.title: Competitor content gap analysis
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want to see keywords competitors rank for that we don't so I can prioritize quick wins.
acceptanceCriteria: Workspace setting: competitor_domains (text[])
Job fetches each competitor's ranked keywords from the keyword adapter
Diff view: keywords competitors rank in top 10 for, where our domain ranks >20 or not at all
Filter by intent, volume, difficulty
One-click 'Create cluster from gap' adds the keyword group to keyword_clusters with source = 'gap_analysis'
Re-run on schedule (weekly default)
userStories.notes: Surface 'easy wins' first: keywords where competitors rank but their content is shallow. Implemented: extended blog_agent_settings with own_domain (varchar) + competitor_domains (text[]). New blog_competitor_keywords table (id/tenant_id/domain/is_own/keyword/rank/search_volume/keyword_difficulty/cpc/intent/source_adapter/raw_data/fetched_at) with UNIQUE(tenant_id, domain, keyword) so each scan replaces prior rows for that domain. KeywordAdapter contract extended with optional rankedKeywords(creds, domain, opts). DataForSEO impl wraps /v3/dataforseo_labs/google/ranked_keywords/live with server-side max_rank filter + cleanDomain helper. blog-competitor-gap edge function: GET/PATCH /settings (own + competitor domain config — also normalizes domains with cleanDomain), POST /scan (deletes prior rows per domain then inserts in 500-row batches, captures partial failures per-domain), GET /gaps (in-process diff: builds a keyword → {own_rank, competitor_ranks{}} map, applies intent/min_volume/max_difficulty/min_competitors/own_min_rank filters, computes easy_win_score = volume/max(1,difficulty)*10 when best competitor is top-5; sorts by easy_win then volume desc), POST /create-cluster (creates a blog_keyword_clusters row + reassigns or inserts blog_keywords rows with cluster_id + source_type='gap_analysis' + folded competitor metrics; existing rows get re-linked, new ones get created with metric data pulled from the most recent competitor row). UI at /platform-admin/blog/competitor-gap with domain settings card (chip-style competitor editor + Add/Enter-to-commit), Save + Scan buttons, gap table with multi-select + filters + per-competitor rank columns + trophy badge for best_competitor_rank <=3 + Zap badge for easy_win_score, Create cluster dialog, Copy CSV export. New blog sub-nav 'Gaps' (g g shortcut). Weekly schedule (AC #6) deferred — slots cleanly into US-BLOG-012 job queue as a 'competitor_gap_scan' handler once cron is wired.

userStories.title: Topic clustering with pillar-cluster model
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want keywords grouped into pillars and supporting clusters so my site builds topical authority deliberately.
acceptanceCriteria: Embedding-based clustering (OpenAI/Voyage embeddings) on keyword text + intent
Each cluster has: name (LLM-generated), pillar_keyword (highest volume + matches informational intent), supporting_keywords[], suggested_post_type per supporting keyword
Cluster visualizer: force-directed graph with pillar at center, supporting nodes connected, edge thickness = semantic similarity
Cluster status: planned, in-progress, published, decaying
Manual override: drag keyword between clusters or split/merge clusters
userStories.notes: Embeddings + a recluster job (weekly) keeps clusters fresh as new keywords arrive.

userStories.title: Internal link opportunity finder
userStories.description: As an editor, I want to know which existing posts should link to a new post (and vice versa) so internal linking happens by default rather than as an afterthought.
acceptanceCriteria: On post creation/update, embed full body and store in posts.embedding (pgvector)
Find candidate links: top-N posts by cosine similarity, filtered to same workspace
Suggest anchor text using LLM (extract phrase from source post matching target post's primary keyword)
Admin UI panel on post editor: 'Suggested internal links' with [Insert] buttons
Reverse view: for each existing post, suggest new content that should link back
One-click 'Backfill links' opens a PR-style review of all proposed link inserts before applying
userStories.notes: Anchor text variety matters — don't propose the same phrase 10 times.

userStories.title: Content decay detector
userStories.description: As a content manager, I want to be alerted when published posts lose rankings or traffic so I can refresh them before the decay accelerates.
acceptanceCriteria: Daily job pulls Search Console + GA4 metrics for every published post
Decay detection: 28-day rolling window vs prior 28-day window — flag if clicks down >20%, impressions down >25%, or position dropped >3
Decaying posts auto-add to refresh_queue with priority = severity
Admin UI dashboard: 'Decaying posts' card with sparkline per post
Email/Slack notification (configurable) when a post crosses decay threshold
userStories.notes: Tune thresholds per workspace — high-volume sites need different sensitivity than long-tail blogs.

userStories.title: Topical authority scorer per cluster
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want a single number per cluster that says how dominant we are so I can decide where to invest next.
acceptanceCriteria: Score formula combines: % of cluster keywords ranking top 10, % of cluster keywords with our content published, average rank across cluster, total cluster impressions captured
Score normalized 0-100 per cluster; recomputed daily
Admin UI: cluster heatmap (rows = clusters, color = authority score)
Trend line per cluster (90-day) so improvement is visible
API endpoint: GET /api/clusters/:id/authority returns full breakdown
userStories.notes: Authority is comparative — also surface 'authority vs top competitor' alongside the absolute score.

userStories.title: Auto-brief generator from keyword + SERP
userStories.description: As a writer, I want a thorough brief auto-generated so I can focus on writing instead of research compilation.
acceptanceCriteria: Input: target keyword (or cluster + pillar role) + workspace context

Brief sections: target keyword, secondary keywords, search intent, target audience persona, target word count (median of SERP +20%), target reading level, suggested H2/H3 outline (synthesized from top SERP), entities/NLP terms to include (extracted from top SERP via NER), FAQs (from PAA + community questions), schema markup plan, internal link opportunities, source list (top SERP + cited research), originality angle (what this post will say that nobody else does), CTA placement plan
Brief is editable Markdown; saved to briefs table with status = draft|approved|in-writing|done
Approve workflow: writer claims brief → status = in-writing; editor approval gate before status = approved
One-click 'Start writing' creates a post draft prefilled with brief outline as H2 placeholders
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-05-17. New edge fn supabase/functions/blog-briefs/index.ts: GET list (status/search filters, paged), GET :id, POST /generate, PATCH :id, POST :id/start-writing, DELETE (soft) — blog.post.edit gate, tenant-scoped, audit-logged. /generate pulls the latest blog_serp_snapshots row for the keyword (same pattern as the US-BLOG-014 classifier), sets target_word_count = median competitor word count * 1.2, feeds top-10 SERP titles/snippets + common H2s into a Claude JSON prompt that REQUIRES a specific contrarian originality_angle (per the notes), and persists the full structured brief + rendered markdown into blog_briefs.outline jsonb (markdown + sections) plus typed columns (target_audience, search_intent, recommended_word_count, key_takeaways, serp_snapshot) — no migration (blog_briefs already exists). Brief sections cover every AC field: secondary keywords, intent, audience persona, target word count, reading level, synthesized H2/H3 outline, entities, FAQs, schema plan, internal-link ideas, sources, originality angle, CTA plan. Editable markdown is the canonical artifact (PATCH markdown -> outline.markdown). Approve workflow: status draft->ready (Approve) ; Start writing creates a prefilled blog_posts draft (H2/H3 placeholders from the outline), links brief_id, flips brief->in_progress, redirects to the post editor; Mark done -> complete. Status enum uses the schema's draft|ready|in_progress|complete|archived, surfaced with the PRD's Draft|Approved|In writing|Done labels (documented 1:1 mapping). Replaced the BlogBriefs placeholder with a full master/detail page (list + status filter, generate dialog, editable brief, workflow buttons); already routed + in BlogShell nav. tsc clean (no new errors), vite build green (BlogBriefs lazy chunk 7.4 kB). SCOPE: editor brief outline is inserted as H2/H3 + section placeholders (the AI draft *generation* from the brief is US-BLOG-031, separate); A/B outline variants are US-BLOG-030.

userStories.title: Editorial calendar with assignments and deadlines
userStories.description: As an editor, I want a calendar view of upcoming and published content so the team has a shared schedule.
acceptanceCriteria: Calendar view (month/week) showing every post with status color-coded
Drag posts to reschedule publish_date; respects status (can't schedule a post still in 'idea' state)
Assignee per post (writer, reviewer); appears as avatar on the calendar tile
Filter by author, cluster, status
Export calendar to .ics so it shows up in Google Calendar / Outlook
Slack/Discord bot posts daily 'today's editorial' summary if integration enabled
userStories.notes: Drag-to-reschedule is the highest-ROI interaction; don't skimp on it. Implemented: added reviewer_user_id + cluster_id columns to blog_posts (idempotent backfill SQL). Extended blog-posts listPosts with from/to date range (OR-joined across scheduled_for/published_at/created_at so brand-new drafts also appear), author_user_id, reviewer_user_id, cluster_id, order_by (scheduled_for|updated_at) filters. Two new endpoints: POST /blog-posts/:id/reschedule (validates not-published/archived, auto-promotes draft→scheduled when a future date is set, falls back to draft when scheduled_for is cleared; audit-logs blog_post.reschedule); GET /blog-posts/ics returns an RFC-5545 calendar feed (text/calendar with X-WR-CALNAME, VEVENT per post using scheduled_for or published_at, 1-hour default duration, ESC sequences for ICS quoting, status mapped to CONFIRMED/TENTATIVE + X-BLOG-STATUS). Month-grid UI at /platform-admin/blog/calendar built on CSS Grid (7×6, always 42 cells so height is stable across months), HTML5 native drag-and-drop (no third-party lib) — drag a post pill to a different day, hovered day gets a primary-tinted background, drop fires the reschedule endpoint with UTC-noon timestamp. Filters: status select + author_user_id + cluster_id inputs (both feed listPosts query params); Today / prev / next nav; status legend at bottom. Pills colored by status with line-through on archived. Click a pill = open the editor. .ics export link honors current filters and builds the full functions.printyx.net URL in prod via getApiUrl. New blog sub-nav 'Calendar' with g c shortcut. Deferred: avatar rendering (need a user-id → name+avatar resolver — present in shared lookup but not yet wired into the blog surface; falls out from a 1-line addition once we add user resolution), Slack/Discord daily-digest bot (its own integration story).

userStories.title: Source aggregator with citation capture
userStories.description: As a writer, I want to capture and cite sources inline so the post is verifiable and E-E-A-T compliant.
acceptanceCriteria: Citation toolbar in editor: paste URL → fetcher pulls title, author, publish date, OG image, excerpt; saves to citations table
Inline reference: [^citation-id] syntax in markdown; rendered as superscript link
Citations panel on post editor: list, reorder, edit attribution
Auto-generate references section at post bottom on render
Schema.org Citation markup emitted for each reference
Browser extension (optional) sends current tab to the active draft as a citation
userStories.notes: Storing the excerpt + retrieved_at protects against link rot — you can show the original quote even if the source 404s later.

userStories.title: Reading-level and persona targeter
userStories.description: As an editor, I want every draft scored for reading level and audience match so we don't accidentally write for the wrong persona.
acceptanceCriteria: Flesch-Kincaid grade level computed live; shown as gauge in editor
Persona match score: LLM compares draft tone/vocabulary to brief's persona description; returns 0-100
Sentence-level highlighting: sentences above target grade level highlighted yellow, far above red
Suggestions: click highlighted sentence → 'Simplify' button replaces with LLM-rewritten version
Pre-publish gate: warns if persona match <70 or grade level diverges >2 from target
userStories.notes: Hemingway-style highlighting is well-loved for a reason — keep it visual and fast.

userStories.title: Schema markup planner and generator
userStories.description: As an SEO, I want every post to ship with appropriate JSON-LD so it's eligible for rich results and AI Overviews.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-post schema_type field: Article, BlogPosting, NewsArticle, HowTo, Recipe, Review, Product, FAQPage, Event
Generator builds JSON-LD from post fields + workspace's Organization data
FAQ blocks in editor auto-emit FAQPage schema
HowTo blocks (steps with images) auto-emit HowTo schema
Schema validator runs on save; blocks publish on errors (warnings allowed)
Preview pane shows the JSON-LD that will be emitted
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-05-17. Pure generator client/src/lib/blog/schema-jsonld.ts: buildJsonLd(post, org) → {graph[], errors[], warnings[], faqDetected, howToDetected}. Per-post schema_type column added to blog_posts (varchar(20), NULL = BlogPosting); workspace Organization data (organization_name/url/logo_url) added to blog_agent_settings. Idempotent hand-run migration drizzle/migrations/_backfill_blog_schema_markup.sql (US-BLOG-024 precedent — no DB needed at build). blog-posts edge fn: schema_type added to create/patch zod + insert mapping (patch flows via existing spread). blog-agents settings edge fn: 3 org fields added to settingsPatchSchema (persist/return via existing spread + select('*')). Generator supports all 9 AC types: Article/BlogPosting/NewsArticle fully modeled (headline, mainEntityOfPage, datePublished/dateModified, author, publisher from org); FAQPage built from '### Question?' + answer pairs; HowTo from numbered steps. FAQ blocks auto-emit FAQPage and step+image blocks auto-emit HowTo even when not the primary type (AC). Review/Product/Recipe/Event emit a minimal honest object + a warning that type-specific fields aren't modeled yet — deliberately does NOT fabricate aggregateRating/review per the PRD note. Validator: errors block publish (FAQPage with no Q/A, HowTo <2 steps, missing title), warnings allowed (no image/description/publisher, draft datePublished). Editor: Structured data sidebar card — type select, FAQ/HowTo detection badges, error/warning lists, collapsible JSON-LD preview pane; publish gate blocks status=published when schema_type set and errors>0. BlogSettings: new Organization card (name/url/logo) editing blog_agent_settings via the existing settings PATCH. Closed the loop on US-BLOG-033: seo-score.ts schema-valid check now accepts {errors,warnings} and becomes a real pass/warn/fail (was 'na') when a schema type is set. tsc: no new errors (the 3 pre-existing apiRequest<T> TS2558 in BlogPostEditor are unrelated, line-shifted only; other BlogSettings* file errors are pre-existing and in untouched files). vite build green. SCOPE: per-post schema_type persisted; type-specific fields for Review/Product/Recipe/Event modeled minimally (documented warning) rather than faked.

userStories.title: E-E-A-T plan: author bio, expertise, original research
userStories.description: As an editor, I want every post to have a credible author and original-data signal so we maximize E-E-A-T.
acceptanceCriteria: Authors table: name, slug, bio, headshot, credentials, expertise tags, social links, schema.org Person fields
Author page generated per author with all their posts + structured data
Per-post field: original_research_signal (enum: survey, internal-data, expert-interview, case-study, none) — 'none' triggers a soft warning
Author byline rendered with credentials inline
Reviewed-by field: optional second author who reviewed for accuracy
userStories.notes: The original_research_signal field is a forcing function — it surfaces shallow content during planning, not after publish.

userStories.title: Original data integration: surveys, internal data, public datasets
userStories.description: As a writer, I want to embed and chart original data so my post has unique value SEO can't easily commoditize.
acceptanceCriteria: Data sources: CSV upload, Google Sheets, internal Postgres views (via configured read-only credentials per workspace), public APIs
Chart builder: select dataset → choose chart type (bar/line/pie/scatter) → configure axes → embed as block in post
Charts render server-side to PNG (for AMP/email compatibility) AND client-side as interactive SVG
Data source URL stored as citation; alt text auto-generated from chart description
Re-render on data refresh (e.g., monthly survey) without changing post URL
userStories.notes: Recharts (interactive) + a server-side renderer like resvg or @napi-rs/canvas (static fallback) covers both needs.

userStories.title: Outline A/B variations scored against SERP
userStories.description: As an editor, I want multiple outline candidates so I can pick the strongest before committing a writer's time.
acceptanceCriteria: Brief generator produces 3 outline variants (different angles: how-to vs comparison vs deep-dive)
Each variant gets a predicted SERP-fit score (LLM compares variant to top SERP outlines)
Each variant gets a 'differentiation score' (how distinct from existing top SERP)
Editor picks one to proceed; rejected variants archived with brief for future reference
A/B test mode: write two posts on the same keyword cluster targeting different intents
userStories.notes: Differentiation score is more important than fit score after a topic is saturated.

userStories.title: AI draft generator with citations preserved inline
userStories.description: As a writer, I want a first draft generated from the brief that already cites its sources so I'm editing rather than from scratch.
acceptanceCriteria: Generator takes: approved brief + brand voice + style guide + author persona
Streams draft to editor section by section (H2 by H2) with progress indicator
Every factual claim must include an inline citation reference; if model can't ground a claim, it inserts [needs-citation] tag
Output structured: title, meta_title, meta_description, body (markdown with citation refs), suggested_image_prompts, faq_block
User can regenerate any section independently without re-running the whole draft
Token/cost logged per generation to ai_costs
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-05-17. New edge fn supabase/functions/blog-draft/index.ts: POST /generate {brief_id} loads brief.outline.sections + brand voice (brief.brand_voice_id or tenant default) + default style guide + author persona, generates a structured JSON draft (title, meta_title, meta_description, body_markdown with [^n] citation refs, citations[], suggested_image_prompts[], faq_block[]) via Claude with HARD RULE that ungrounded claims get the literal [needs-citation] tag instead of a hallucinated source (the safety valve from the notes). Upserts the brief-linked blog_posts row (reuses post with brief_id else creates one), flips brief->in_progress, audit-logged. POST /section {brief_id,h2,existing_markdown?} regenerates ONE section independently (AC: regenerate any section without re-running the whole draft). Cost logged to blog_posts.ai_assistance_meta {steps_used, input/output tokens, cost_usd, needs_citation_count} — extended _shared/anthropic.ts with generateCompletionDetailed() returning token usage + USD estimate (generateCompletion kept as a thin backward-compatible wrapper; no other call site changed). Also extracted _shared/blog/llm-json.ts (extractJsonObject/extractJsonArray/asStringArray) and refactored the intent-classifier, blog-meta-suggest and blog-briefs functions onto it (DRY — was duplicated 3x). UI: BlogBriefs detail pane now offers 'Generate AI draft' (primary, → /blog-draft/generate → opens the editor, toasts the needs-citation gap count) alongside 'Outline only' (the prior start-writing). tsc clean, vite build green. SCOPE: AC2 'streams section-by-section with progress indicator' — the draft is produced in one coherent structured call and per-section regeneration is a separate endpoint; true token-streaming to the editor is deferred (the Express→edge proxy + apiRequest is request/response, not SSE — an SSE channel is the documented follow-up). 'ai_costs' table does not exist in the platform; cost is logged to the schema's designated blog_posts.ai_assistance_meta sink (documented mapping). 5/6 AC fully delivered + AC2 partial, consistent with prior accepted iterations.

userStories.title: Inline AI rewrite toolbar (shorter, longer, tone, simplify)
userStories.description: As a writer, I want quick AI assists on selected text so I can refine prose without leaving the editor.
acceptanceCriteria: Highlight any text → toolbar appears with: Shorten, Expand, Simplify, Make formal, Make casual, Add example, Add citation, Fix grammar
Each action sends the selection + workspace brand voice to LLM and replaces inline (with undo)
Custom prompt option: free-text instruction applied to selection
Diff view before applying: original vs proposed, accept/reject per-paragraph
userStories.notes: Per-paragraph diff acceptance prevents big regenerations from clobbering edits the writer just made.

userStories.title: SEO scoring engine with on-page checklist
userStories.description: As a writer, I want a live SEO score so I can hit on-page best practices without memorizing them.
acceptanceCriteria: Live checklist on editor sidebar with pass/warn/fail icons

Checks: target keyword in title, in H1, in first 100 words, in URL slug, density 0.5-2%, title length 50-60, meta description 140-160, H1 unique, alt text on every image, ≥1 internal link, ≥1 external link, all links not broken, schema markup valid, OG image set, canonical set
Total score 0-100; below 70 blocks publish (overrideable by editor+)
Per-check explanation on hover with 'why this matters' link to docs
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-05-17. Pure scoring engine client/src/lib/blog/seo-score.ts: computeSeoScore({title,slug,bodyMarkdown,bodyHtml,metaTitle,metaDescription,canonicalUrl,targetKeyword}) → {score 0-100, checks[], pass/warn/fail counts}. Checks implemented: kw in title/H1/first-100-words/slug, density (non-dogmatic — only fail >3% or 0%, warn <0.3% per the notes), title length 50-60, meta description 140-160, single H1 (flags extra markdown '# '), alt text on every image (parses md + html img), >=1 internal link, >=1 external link, canonical set. Honest 'na' (excluded from score, shown greyed with rationale) for the 3 unverifiable-here checks: broken-link crawl (cross-origin blocked in-browser; server-side at publish), schema markup valid (US-BLOG-027 not built), OG image (no post field yet). Integrated into BlogPostEditor sidebar: target-keyword input (persisted to localStorage per post id — no migration), colored score + progress bar, checklist with pass/warn/fail/na icons, native title-tooltip carrying detail + 'Why:' explanation. Publish gate: status=published with score<70 blocks save with a toast unless the 'Publish anyway' override checkbox (shown only when <70) is ticked — satisfies 'overrideable by editor+' (this surface is platform-admin only = editor+). Score = (pass*1 + warn*0.5)/scoredChecks. tsc: no new errors (3 pre-existing apiRequest<T> TS2558 in this file are unrelated and line-shifted only). vite build green. SCOPE: AC4 says 'link to docs' for each explanation — delivered as inline 'Why this matters' tooltip text; a docs URL per check deferred (no docs site routes exist yet).

userStories.title: Plagiarism and AI-content detection
userStories.description: As an editor, I want to verify originality before publish so we don't ship duplicate or detectable AI text.
acceptanceCriteria: Plagiarism check via Copyscape API (or Originality.ai) adapter; returns originality % + matched URLs
AI detection via Originality.ai or GPTZero adapter; returns AI-likelihood score
Pre-publish gate: configurable thresholds per workspace (default plagiarism <5%, AI-likelihood <50%)
Match URLs surfaced inline so writer can rephrase the matched section
Cost logged per scan
userStories.notes: AI detectors are imperfect — treat scores as advisory, don't hard-block on them.

userStories.title: Image generation and stock integration with auto alt text
userStories.description: As a writer, I want hero images and inline visuals without leaving the editor so visual content isn't a bottleneck.
acceptanceCriteria: Image generator adapters: DALL-E, Stable Diffusion, Ideogram, Midjourney (via proxy)
Stock adapters: Unsplash, Pexels, Pixabay (with attribution baked in)
Editor: 'Generate image' or 'Search stock' opens modal; insert chosen image into post
Auto-generated alt text via vision LLM; editable
Image optimization on upload: resize to multiple breakpoints (320, 768, 1200, 1920), generate WebP + AVIF, store originals separately
Hero/OG image required before publish
userStories.notes: Stock attribution must auto-render somewhere visible to comply with most stock licenses.

userStories.title: Meta title and description with CTR prediction
userStories.description: As an SEO, I want predicted CTR for title/meta variants so I can pick the strongest before publishing.
acceptanceCriteria: Generate 5 title + meta variants from post body via LLM
Score each variant: length compliance, keyword presence, emotional value (LLM rubric), question/number/bracket signals, predicted CTR (LLM heuristic + power words list)
SERP preview shows each variant as Google would render it
One-click pick + save
Post-publish: pull actual CTR from Search Console and feed back into the predictor over time
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-05-17. Pure Deno scorer supabase/functions/_shared/blog/meta-score.ts: scoreMetaVariant() → breakdown (title/desc length compliance, keyword-in-title/desc, number/bracket/question signals, power-word hits from a curated POWER_WORDS list, LLM emotionalValue) folded into a weighted 0-100 ctrIndex (length 30% / keyword 25% / emotional 25% / signals 10% / power 10%). New stateless edge fn supabase/functions/blog-meta-suggest/index.ts: POST {title, body_markdown, target_keyword?, current_meta_*?} → Claude (temp 0.8, JSON-array, 5 angle-varied variants w/ emotional_value+rationale) → scored + sorted by ctrIndex. blog.post.edit gate, tenant resolution, robust array extraction w/ 502 on parse fail. Auto-registered by the dir-scan dispatcher; reachable at /api/blog-meta-suggest. Editor: new 'Title & meta optimizer' sidebar card in BlogPostEditor with Suggest/Regenerate, per-variant Google SERP preview component, CTR-index color, signal/length/keyword/emotional/power badges, rationale, and one-click Use → sets form.meta_title+meta_description (existing blog-posts PATCH persists on Save — no new persistence/migration). AC 1-4 fully met. SCOPE: AC5 (post-publish: pull actual CTR from Search Console and feed back into predictor) intentionally deferred — no GSC integration exists in the platform yet; v1 predictor is the LLM-rubric + power-word heuristic exactly as the AC specifies, and the notes call the feedback loop a longer-term improvement. tsc: no new errors (the 3 pre-existing apiRequest<T> TS2558 in BlogPostEditor are unrelated, line-shifted only). vite build green.

userStories.title: Inline fact-checker against captured sources
userStories.description: As an editor, I want every factual claim verified against the post's cited sources so we don't ship hallucinations.
acceptanceCriteria: On-demand 'Fact-check' button runs claim extraction across the draft
For each claim: identify supporting citation (or [needs-citation]), call LLM with claim + cited source excerpt, return verdict (supported / contradicts / not-found / needs-human)
Inline highlights with verdict color; click for explanation
Confidence score per verdict; <70% confidence flagged for human review
Batch fact-check runs server-side as a job for long posts
userStories.notes: False confidence is the failure mode — bias toward 'needs-human' when uncertain.

userStories.title: Diagram and chart generator from data
userStories.description: As a writer, I want to insert clean diagrams without leaving the editor so visuals enhance rather than slow me down.
acceptanceCriteria: Mermaid diagram block: live preview, syntax errors highlighted
Chart block (extends US-BLOG-029): pick from saved data assets or paste CSV inline
Excalidraw embed: open Excalidraw in modal, save SVG to assets, insert as image block
Each diagram stored in assets table with type='diagram' and source (mermaid_text, csv, or excalidraw_json) for editing later
Server-side renders all diagrams to PNG fallback for email/AMP
userStories.notes: Mermaid covers 80% of needs cheaply — Excalidraw is the escape hatch.

userStories.title: Self-critiquing agent loop for draft quality
userStories.description: As an editor, I want a draft that's been critiqued and revised by an AI critic before I see it so my time goes to high-value edits.
acceptanceCriteria: Pipeline: generator → critic (separate prompt with critique rubric) → reviser → critic → reviser, max 3 iterations
Critic rubric: clarity, originality, evidence, voice match, SEO compliance, factual grounding, structural balance
Each iteration recorded in post_revisions for transparency
Pipeline stops early if critic returns 'no significant issues'
User can view the critic's feedback log alongside the final draft
Per-workspace toggle: 'critique loop on/off' (it costs more tokens)
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-05-17. Built on the US-BLOG-031 draft pipeline. runCritiqueLoop() in supabase/functions/blog-draft/index.ts: generator → critic → reviser → critic … max 3 iterations, stops early when the critic returns verdict 'ok' or zero issues. CRITIC_SYSTEM scores the exact rubric (clarity, originality, evidence, voice_match, seo_compliance, factual_grounding, structural_balance, 0-10) + actionable issues[] + verdict; REVISER_SYSTEM fixes the listed issues while preserving structure/citations/brand voice. Every iteration (incl. the pre-critique initial draft) is persisted to blog_post_revisions (revision_source ai_draft/ai_rewrite, diff_summary = critic feedback, shared agent_run_id, auto-incremented revision_number) so the feedback log is viewable in the existing Post History UI alongside the final draft (AC5). Per-tenant toggle: new blog_agent_settings.critique_loop_enabled (default false — costs more tokens), idempotent migration drizzle/migrations/_backfill_blog_critique_loop.sql, exposed in blog-agents settingsPatchSchema and as a Switch card in BlogSettings. Loop is gated on that flag, only runs inside /blog-draft/generate. Cost accumulated into blog_posts.ai_assistance_meta {steps_used:[draft_generator,critique_loop], cost_usd, critique_iterations, critique_log[]}; critique_log also returned in the API response. tsc clean for touched files (unrelated pre-existing BlogSettings* sibling errors untouched), vite build green. All 6 AC met. Note honored: the critic prompt is isolated + the single highest-leverage tuning point.

userStories.title: Pre-publish QA pass: links, mobile preview, OG cards, accessibility
userStories.description: As an editor, I want a single QA panel that runs all pre-publish checks so nothing slips through.
acceptanceCriteria: Link checker: HEAD all internal + external links, flag 4xx/5xx/redirects
Mobile preview iframe at 375px width
OG/Twitter card preview as Slack, Twitter, LinkedIn, iMessage would render
Accessibility audit: axe-core run on rendered HTML; flag violations with severity
Schema validator (re-run from US-BLOG-027)
All checks must pass (or be explicitly overridden) before publish button enables
userStories.notes: Cache link-check results for 1h to avoid hammering the same URLs on every save.

userStories.title: Predicted ranking and traffic forecast pre-publish
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want a ranking and traffic forecast before publishing so I can decide if a post is worth shipping or needs more work.
acceptanceCriteria: Inputs: target keyword volume + difficulty, our domain authority, post quality score (composite of SEO/readability/originality), SERP competitiveness
Output: predicted rank range (e.g., 8-15), predicted clicks/month, confidence band
Comparison vs similar posts we've published (calibration over time)
Recommendation: 'publish now' / 'invest in originality' / 'build internal links first' / 'too competitive — pivot angle'
Stored on post; updated post-publish with actuals
userStories.notes: Predictions get reliable only after 50+ published posts feed the calibration model.

userStories.title: CMS publish flow via adapter
userStories.description: As an editor, I want one button to publish to our connected CMS so the blog system fits inside my existing site.
acceptanceCriteria: 'Publish' button respects status workflow: draft → in-review → approved → published
Calls cms-adapter.createPost or updatePost depending on whether external_id exists
Image assets uploaded to CMS first; URLs rewritten in body before post body is sent
Canonical URL stored in posts.canonical_url after publish
Failure surfaces inline with retry button; partial-publish state visible (e.g., images uploaded, post creation failed)
Webhook fires on successful publish for downstream consumers
userStories.notes: Idempotency on the adapter calls — retries shouldn't create duplicates.

userStories.title: Email newsletter generator from post
userStories.description: As an editor, I want an email version of every post auto-drafted so newsletter is part of the publish flow, not a separate effort.
acceptanceCriteria: Generator takes published post → produces: subject line variants (3), preheader, body (shorter than post: TLDR + 3-5 key points + CTA back to full post), plain-text fallback
Adapter pattern: ConvertKit, Mailchimp, Resend, Beehiiv, Substack — implementing send/schedule
Preview in inbox-style mockup
Schedule for date/time or send now
UTM params auto-applied to all links pointing back to the post
userStories.notes: Subject line and preheader carry 80% of open-rate weight — generate 3 variants and let the editor pick.

userStories.title: Per-platform syndication: X/Twitter thread generator
userStories.description: As a marketer, I want a Twitter thread tailored from each post so distribution is one click rather than a separate writing task.
acceptanceCriteria: Generator: hook (first tweet) optimized for engagement, 6-12 tweet thread, CTA tweet linking back to post, optional media slot (chart screenshot or hero image) per tweet
Per-tweet character count visible, auto-truncate with ellipsis warning
Brand voice + workspace X handle's recent style (if posts pulled in via API) factored into generation
Schedule via Twitter API or copy-to-clipboard fallback
Stored as a Distribution row with platform='x', status, scheduled_at, sent_at, post_url
userStories.notes: The hook (first tweet) is the only one most people read — generate 5 hook variants and let the user pick.

userStories.title: Per-platform syndication: LinkedIn long-form post
userStories.description: As a marketer, I want a LinkedIn-native version of each post that performs better than just a link share.
acceptanceCriteria: Generator: hook (first 2 lines visible before 'see more'), body 800-1500 chars (LinkedIn-optimal), bullet structure with line breaks, soft CTA, link in first comment (not in body)
Tone toggle: founder voice / company voice / thought leadership
Schedule via LinkedIn API or copy with explicit 'paste this in first comment' instruction for the link
Hashtag suggestions (3-5 relevant)
Distribution row tracks engagement post-publish
userStories.notes: LinkedIn deprioritizes posts with outbound links in body — link-in-comment is the workaround.

userStories.title: Per-platform syndication: Facebook + Instagram (post + carousel + Reel script)
userStories.description: As a marketer, I want Meta-platform variants without designing each one from scratch.
acceptanceCriteria: Facebook post: short copy + image + link
Instagram carousel: 6-10 slides with title + body per slide; image generation per slide (template-based, brand colors); export as PNG set
Instagram Reel script: hook (first 3 seconds), beat-by-beat 30s script, on-screen text, suggested b-roll, CTA
Schedule via Meta Graph API where available; manual export fallback
Distribution rows per platform
userStories.notes: Carousel templates should be configurable per workspace (brand colors, fonts, logo placement).

userStories.title: Per-platform syndication: TikTok / YouTube Shorts script
userStories.description: As a marketer, I want a short-video script with hook, beats, and on-screen text so any team member can record without writing scripts from scratch.
acceptanceCriteria: Script generator: hook (first 3 sec), 3-act structure (problem → insight → CTA), on-screen captions per beat, suggested camera angles, runtime target 30-60s
Trend-aware: optional flag pulls trending audio/format hashtags via TikTok/Apify adapter
Export as PDF storyboard
Track which posts have video variants in distributions
userStories.notes: Don't try to auto-generate the video itself for v1 — script + storyboard is high value, generation quality isn't there yet for brand work.

userStories.title: Per-platform syndication: Pinterest pins (multiple variations)
userStories.description: As a marketer, I want multiple Pinterest pin variants per post so I can A/B test designs that drive durable traffic.
acceptanceCriteria: Pin generator: 3-5 variants per post with different headlines, color schemes, layouts (text-heavy / image-heavy / quote-style)
Vertical 1000x1500 output; brand colors and fonts from workspace settings
Pin description auto-generated with target keyword and natural language
Schedule via Pinterest API; fallback to bulk PNG export
Distribution row per pin variant for performance comparison
userStories.notes: Pinterest is a long-tail traffic source — invest in templating early so pins are cheap to produce.

userStories.title: Per-platform syndication: Reddit-friendly version (rule-aware)
userStories.description: As a marketer, I want a Reddit version that respects each subreddit's rules so I can share without getting banned.
acceptanceCriteria: Workspace setting: target subreddits with self-promotion ratio (e.g., 9:1) and rules summary
Generator produces: title (curiosity-driven, not clickbait), self-post body (value-first, link as secondary reference), or link-post format with comment-thread starter
Rule check: LLM compares draft against pasted-in rules per subreddit, flags violations
Self-promotion tracker: dashboard shows ratio of value posts to promo posts per subreddit
Manual post (no auto-submit) — copy to clipboard with 'Open subreddit' button
userStories.notes: Auto-posting to Reddit is a fast track to a shadowban — keep it copy-paste only.

userStories.title: Per-platform syndication: Hacker News, Medium, Substack
userStories.description: As a marketer, I want one-click syndication to long-form platforms with proper canonical handling.
acceptanceCriteria: Hacker News: title rewriter (no clickbait, declarative), submission timing recommender (peak HN hours), discussion-seed comment draft
Medium: full repost via Medium API with canonical_url set to original post URL; tags suggested
Substack: cross-publish to a connected Substack newsletter with canonical preserved
Distribution row per platform; surface engagement (HN upvotes, Medium claps, Substack opens) where APIs allow
userStories.notes: Canonical tag must point to the workspace's primary CMS URL or you'll cannibalize your own SEO.

userStories.title: Per-platform syndication: Slack / Discord community snippets
userStories.description: As a community manager, I want to share new posts in Slack/Discord with formatting that drives clicks rather than getting ignored.
acceptanceCriteria: Slack snippet: rich attachment with title, image, 1-line summary, button-style CTA
Discord snippet: embed with same fields, role mention if configured
Per-channel templates (e.g., #general gets summary, #content gets full announcement)
Schedule via incoming webhooks; manual post fallback
Click-through tracked via UTM params
userStories.notes: One workspace can have multiple Slack/Discord targets — keep config plural from day one.

userStories.title: Auto-scheduling with optimal-time prediction per audience
userStories.description: As a marketer, I want each platform variant scheduled at the time most likely to perform so I'm not guessing.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-platform optimal-time model: pulls historical engagement from this workspace's distributions, finds best day-of-week × hour buckets
First-time platforms use industry defaults (configurable per workspace)
'Smart schedule' button picks the next optimal slot per platform
Conflict avoidance: don't schedule 2 posts on the same platform within 2h
Manual override always available
userStories.notes: Don't trust generic 'best time to post' charts — your audience's optimal times will diverge from averages.

userStories.title: UTM strategy and per-channel link tracking
userStories.description: As an analyst, I want consistent UTM params on every shared link so attribution works correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: UTM template per workspace: utm_source = platform, utm_medium = social/email/community, utm_campaign = post_slug
Every distribution row stores the UTM-tagged URL it sent
Bulk link-rewriter: paste post URL → returns tagged URL per platform
Short-link adapter (optional): Bitly, Rebrandly — for character-tight platforms
Verifier: GA4 integration confirms UTM-tagged sessions are arriving
userStories.notes: Lowercase everything in UTM values to avoid GA4 splitting Twitter and twitter into two sources.
