userStories.title: Re-share cadence engine
userStories.description: As a marketer, I want each post to be re-shared on a schedule that surfaces value without spamming so evergreen content gets full lifetime traffic.
acceptanceCriteria: Default cadence: T+0 (publish day all platforms), T+3 (re-hook on X), T+7 (LinkedIn fresh angle), T+30 (community resurface), T+90, T+180
Each scheduled re-share generates a new variant (different hook) automatically
Stops auto-scheduling if engagement on prior re-shares is below threshold
Editor can pause/resume cadence per post
Distribution timeline view per post shows past + scheduled future shares
userStories.notes: Re-shares fail when they're identical to the original — variation is mandatory, not optional.

userStories.title: Internal-link auto-injection on publish
userStories.description: As an editor, I want existing posts auto-linked to a newly published pillar so internal linking compounds without manual backfill.
acceptanceCriteria: On publish of a post tagged as pillar, find top-N existing posts with high semantic similarity AND no link to the new pillar
Generate proposed anchor + sentence-level edits to insert the link naturally
Editor reviews proposed edits in PR-style diff view; accept all / reject all / per-change accept
Accepted edits create new revisions on those posts and re-publish via CMS adapter
Backlink count surfaced on the new pillar's stats card
userStories.notes: Keep human-in-the-loop on auto-injection — silent edits to published posts are a trust killer.

userStories.title: Backlink monitoring and lost-link recovery
userStories.description: As an SEO, I want to know when backlinks appear or disappear so I can capitalize on momentum and recover lost links.
acceptanceCriteria: Backlink adapter: Ahrefs, SEMrush, Majestic — implementing newBacklinks, lostBacklinks per domain
Daily job pulls deltas; new backlinks logged, lost backlinks added to recovery queue with last-seen URL
Recovery workflow: draft outreach email to the lost-link domain explaining the broken link and suggesting our updated URL
Notifications on high-DA new links (configurable threshold) so the marketing team can amplify
Backlink trend chart per post
userStories.notes: Lost-link recovery converts ~15-25% on a good day — well worth the automation.

userStories.title: Unlinked brand-mention monitor → outreach
userStories.description: As an SEO, I want unlinked mentions of our brand surfaced so I can convert them to backlinks.
acceptanceCriteria: Mention monitor: Google Alerts API alternative (Brand24, Mention.com, or scrape) — finds mentions of brand name across web
Filter: pages where brand is mentioned but no link to our domain
Per mention: propose outreach email contextualizing the mention and politely requesting a link
Outreach status tracker: sent, replied, link-added, declined, ghosted
Auto-detect when link is added (re-crawl mentioned URLs weekly) and update status
userStories.notes: Personalize the outreach with the actual mention quote — generic templates get ignored.

userStories.title: Outreach list generator (sites that linked to similar content)
userStories.description: As an SEO, I want a list of sites likely to link to my new post so outreach has high hit rates.
acceptanceCriteria: Input: published post + 3-5 similar competitor URLs
Pull backlink lists for competitor URLs via backlink adapter
Filter: high DA, content site (not directories), niche relevance score (LLM evaluates target site)
Find contact: hunter.io / clearbit / scrape contact pages
Output: prioritized outreach list with email, role, suggested angle per recipient
userStories.notes: Niche relevance score filter is what separates this from generic backlink scraping.

userStories.title: HARO / Help-A-B2B-Writer pitch generator
userStories.description: As a brand authority builder, I want to respond to HARO-style queries faster than the field so we get cited in major publications.
acceptanceCriteria: Inbound: HARO email parser (forward HARO emails to a workspace inbox; parse into queries)
For each query: match against author expertise tags, draft a pitch using author's bio + relevant past posts as evidence
Pitch format follows HARO conventions (bio, response, contact info)
Editor reviews pitch → approves → sends from workspace email
Track pitch status: sent, replied, included, ignored — feeds calibration of which queries are worth pursuing
userStories.notes: Speed wins HARO — be ready to send within 1h of the email landing.

userStories.title: Outreach agent: research + draft + track replies
userStories.description: As a marketer, I want an agent that handles the cold-email cycle so I'm reviewing relationships, not drafting templates.
acceptanceCriteria: Per outreach target: agent researches recipient (recent posts, social, mutual connections), drafts personalized email, queues for human approval
Approved emails sent via SMTP/SendGrid/Resend adapter from workspace domain
Reply detection via IMAP or webhook; agent classifies reply (interested / decline / question / out-of-office) and proposes next action
Cadence: follow-up 1 at +5d, follow-up 2 at +10d, then close as no-response
Engagement metrics per template/angle so the system learns what works
userStories.notes: Sending from a marketing subdomain (not the primary domain) protects deliverability if the cadence is too aggressive.

userStories.title: GA4 + Search Console integration
userStories.description: As an analyst, I want every post's performance pulled in automatically so I don't switch tabs to check numbers.
acceptanceCriteria: GA4 Data API: pull sessions, users, engagement_time, conversions per post URL daily
Search Console API: pull clicks, impressions, CTR, average position per post URL daily
Backfill 16 months on initial connect (Search Console max), 90 days for GA4
Per-workspace OAuth flow to connect properties
Metrics stored in performance_metrics table; surfaced on post detail page
Trend charts (28-day, 90-day, all-time) per post
userStories.notes: Search Console rate limits are tight — batch requests by date range, not by URL.

userStories.title: Performance dashboard: posts, clusters, channels
userStories.description: As an editor, I want a unified dashboard so I can answer 'how is content doing?' in one glance.
acceptanceCriteria: Top-level cards: total organic clicks (28d), top-performing posts, declining posts, conversions attributed
Per-cluster table: clicks, impressions, average position, # posts, authority score
Per-channel table (from distributions): clicks, sessions, conversions
Date range selector with comparison (vs prior period)
Export CSV per view
userStories.notes: Default the dashboard to 'last 28 days vs prior 28' — that's the comparison most editors want.

userStories.title: Content refresh queue with auto-flagged decay candidates
userStories.description: As a content manager, I want a prioritized refresh queue so the most decay-prone posts get attention first.
acceptanceCriteria: Queue auto-populated by US-BLOG-021 (decay detector) + manual additions
Each queue item: post, decay severity, suggested edits (LLM diffs current SERP vs current post), estimated effort
Click 'Start refresh' opens the post editor with suggested edits as inline annotations
Refresh updates posts.last_refreshed_at; tracked separately from publish_date
After refresh, monitor for ranking recovery; auto-close queue item on recovery
userStories.notes: Refreshing the title + intro + adding new sections recovers most decay; full rewrites are rarely needed.

userStories.title: A/B testing for titles, meta descriptions, CTAs
userStories.description: As an SEO, I want to test on-page elements so improvements are measured, not assumed.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-post experiments: variant A (current) vs variant B (proposed)
Title/meta tests: split-test by alternating variants weekly; compare CTR from Search Console
CTA tests: client-side variant assignment (cookie-based) with conversion tracking
Statistical significance calculator surfaces winner when n is sufficient
Winner auto-promoted (with editor approval) after threshold reached
userStories.notes: Search Console attribution lags 2-3 days — bake that into significance calc.

userStories.title: Cohort analysis: topic → revenue / signups
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want to know which topics drive business outcomes so investment shifts toward what works.
acceptanceCriteria: Conversion definition per workspace (signup, purchase, demo request) configured via GA4 conversion event
Attribution model: last-non-direct-click default; configurable to first-touch or linear
Cohort table: cluster → sessions → conversions → revenue (or signup count)
Time-to-conversion histogram per cluster
ROI per cluster: cost (writing + tools) vs revenue
userStories.notes: Most teams discover ~20% of clusters drive ~80% of revenue — cohort analysis makes the cut decision obvious.

userStories.title: Auto-refresh agent — fully autonomous SERP-decay-triggered re-editing
userStories.description: As a platform admin, I want the auto-refresh agent to detect SERP decay and re-edit posts WITHOUT human review (per scope decision 5D), with every change captured in the audit log and revertable, so content stays competitive without operator overhead.
acceptanceCriteria: Auto-refresh agent runs on a schedule (cron via Supabase scheduled functions) and via blog_refresh_queue triggers

For each candidate post, the agent: (1) re-runs SERP analysis, (2) diffs against the prior SERP snapshot, (3) generates revised sections, (4) commits a new revision to blog_post_revisions with revision_source="auto_refresh_agent", (5) re-publishes via the configured CMS adapter, (6) writes a blog_audit_log entry summarizing what changed and why
No human-approval step in the default path; admin can opt back into manual review per-tenant via a flag on a new blog_agent_settings row (auto_refresh_requires_review boolean, default false)

Hard guardrails: agent will NOT auto-publish if (a) the predicted change exceeds N% of the post body (configurable, default 40%), (b) the SEO score would drop, or (c) brand-voice or style-guide violations are introduced — these cases land in a review queue surfaced on the Refresh page
Every auto-refresh run respects the global agent kill switch (US-BLOG-086) — if paused, run is skipped and a blog_audit_log entry records the skip
Cost-per-run captured in the AI cost dashboard (US-BLOG-079)
Integration test: simulate SERP decay → assert revision created → assert CMS adapter called → assert audit log entry exists
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Source PRD: blog-system-prd.json US-BLOG-066 (elevated from "proposed edits" to "autonomous re-editing" per scope decision 5D). Full autonomy in production requires the kill switch in US-BLOG-086 to land first.

userStories.title: LLM citation graph analyzer (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews)
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want to know which of our posts get cited by AI systems and which competitor posts dominate the citation graph for our keywords.
acceptanceCriteria: Adapter pattern: chatgpt-search, perplexity, google-ai-overview probes — each takes a query, returns the cited URLs
For each tracked keyword cluster, run probes weekly; log citations to llm_citations table
Dashboard: 'AI citation share of voice' per cluster — % of probes citing our domain vs competitors
Diff view: queries where we appear in classic SERP top 10 but NOT in AI citations — hot opportunity list
Per-post AI citation count surfaced alongside organic metrics
userStories.notes: Probing has cost — sample queries, don't probe every keyword every day. Weekly per cluster is plenty.

userStories.title: Answer-Engine Optimization (AEO) chunk structuring
userStories.description: As an SEO, I want every post structured for LLM citation so AI engines can extract clean answers from our content.
acceptanceCriteria: Pre-publish AEO score: checks for self-contained paragraphs (each answers a discrete question), question-shaped H3s, explicit definitions, factual statements with dates and named entities, original-data callouts
Auto-suggest: rewrite vague paragraphs into self-contained answer chunks
Append a 'Quick answers' section at post top with bullet-form direct answers to top PAA questions
Schema.org QAPage / FAQPage applied to those sections
AEO score visible alongside SEO score
userStories.notes: AI Overviews citations correlate with self-contained, well-attributed paragraphs. Optimize for chunk-level quality, not just article-level.

userStories.title: Domain knowledge graph of entities and relationships
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want a knowledge graph of our domain so I can see entity coverage gaps and plan content accordingly.
acceptanceCriteria: NER pipeline extracts entities (people, organizations, products, concepts, locations, dates) from every published post
Entities stored with type, frequency, first/last seen, related posts
Co-occurrence graph: entities mentioned together get edges weighted by co-mention frequency
Visualizer: force-directed graph with cluster-based coloring
Gap detector: entities competitors cover that we don't — added to keyword cluster planning
userStories.notes: Use a small NER model (spaCy or a fine-tuned small LLM) — calling GPT-4 for NER on every post is overkill and expensive.

userStories.title: Real-time SERP monitor with auto-refresh triggers
userStories.description: As an SEO, I want immediate alerts on SERP volatility for our top keywords so I can react before competitors capitalize.
acceptanceCriteria: Hourly SERP polling for tier-1 keywords (configurable list, default top 50 by traffic)
Volatility detection: rank change >3 positions, new SERP feature appearing, new competitor entering top 10
Alert channels: email, Slack, in-app notification — configurable per workspace
Auto-trigger: significant volatility on a published post adds it to refresh_queue with high priority
Volatility timeline per keyword for retrospective analysis
userStories.notes: Hourly polling is expensive — limit to tier-1 keywords. Daily for everything else.

userStories.title: Competitor publishing alerts with response brief
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want to be alerted when a key competitor publishes on a topic we own so I can respond fast.
acceptanceCriteria: Competitor RSS/sitemap monitoring per workspace (add competitor blog URLs)
New posts detected within 24h; LLM summarizes and tags with relevant keyword cluster
Alert if new competitor post targets a keyword we rank for
Auto-generate response brief: what they covered, what we should add or counter, suggested response post angle
One-click 'Create brief from response' adds to brief queue
userStories.notes: Most competitors update their sitemap.xml in real time — that's faster and lower-friction than scraping.

userStories.title: Audience-specific personalized variants from one master doc
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want one master article with multiple audience variants so we serve different ICPs without writing 3 articles.
acceptanceCriteria: Per post: define audience variants (e.g., 'engineer', 'manager', 'executive')
Each variant: different intro, different examples, different CTA, but shares the core body
Variant rendering: server-side personalization based on URL param, cookie segment, or referrer
Schema-aware: only one canonical URL; variants don't get separate URLs (avoid dup content)
Performance per variant tracked separately
userStories.notes: Server-side rendering with edge personalization (Cloudflare Workers, Vercel edge) is the right delivery mechanism. Don't index variant URLs.

userStories.title: Multi-agent draft pipeline: research → outline → draft → fact-check → critic → polish
userStories.description: As an editor, I want a chained agent pipeline that produces near-final drafts so human review focuses on judgment, not basics.
acceptanceCriteria: Pipeline stages as separate prompts/agents: researcher (gathers sources), outliner (structures from sources), drafter (writes from outline), fact-checker (verifies claims), critic (rubric-based critique), polisher (final pass)
Each stage's output stored as an artifact for transparency
Failures at any stage halt pipeline with explanation; resume from failed stage after fix
Cost + latency logged per stage
Per-workspace toggle: which stages to run (cost vs quality tradeoff)
userStories.notes: Pipeline output should always be reviewable as artifacts — opaque agent chains are debugging nightmares.

userStories.title: Programmatic SEO: templated pages from data
userStories.description: As a growth marketer, I want to generate hundreds of templated pages from a dataset so we capture long-tail traffic systematically.
acceptanceCriteria: Template engine: Markdown template with {{variables}}; data source = CSV upload, Google Sheet, internal Postgres view
Variables: any field from data row (e.g., {{city}}, {{product}}, {{stat}})
Per-template: SEO config (title pattern, meta pattern, schema type), brand voice, output destination (CMS adapter)
Quality gate: template + data row run through SEO scorer; rows scoring <70 flagged for manual review or skipped
Bulk publish job with rate limiting (e.g., 50/hour) to avoid CMS overload
Bulk update / unpublish workflows when data changes
userStories.notes: Programmatic SEO without quality gates = doorway pages = manual penalty. Always gate on uniqueness + value per page.

userStories.title: Interactive content blocks: calculators, quizzes, tools
userStories.description: As a marketer, I want to embed interactive tools in posts so we generate utility-driven backlinks.
acceptanceCriteria: Block types: calculator (formula + input fields → output), quiz (question + answer scoring → result), comparison tool, ROI estimator
No-code builder: drag inputs, define formula, configure result text
Embedded as iframe (or inline component if same domain) with tracking
Lead capture (optional): email gate before showing result
Engagement metrics: completion rate, share rate, conversion rate per tool
userStories.notes: Calculators are the highest-ROI interactive content for B2B — they earn backlinks for years.

userStories.title: Multimodal output: podcast TTS + video script + social clips
userStories.description: As a marketer, I want every post repurposed into audio/video automatically so content reaches non-readers.
acceptanceCriteria: Podcast: ElevenLabs/PlayHT TTS adapter; full post narrated with brand voice clone (if licensed); chapter markers from H2s
Output to MP3 + RSS feed (per workspace) for podcast distribution
Video script: structured beats from post; integrate with HeyGen/Synthesia adapter for avatar video (optional)
Social clips: 30-60s audio clips of key insights for IG audiograms / LinkedIn audio posts
Each output stored as asset linked to source post
userStories.notes: Voice cloning requires explicit consent + license — gate behind a 'voice license uploaded' flag per author.

userStories.title: Localization and translation pipeline
userStories.description: As an international team, I want every post translatable into target locales with proper SEO so we capture global search.
acceptanceCriteria: Locale enum per workspace (e.g., en-US, es-MX, de-DE)
Translation adapter: DeepL, Google Translate, GPT-4 — implementing translate(text, source, target, glossary)
Per-locale brand voice variant (different tone for different markets)
Glossary: workspace-specific terms not to translate (brand names, product names)
Hreflang tags emitted on every post; sitemap split per locale
Locale-specific publish flow: each translation has its own status, reviewer, publish_date
userStories.notes: Don't auto-publish translations without native review — machine translation is good for v1 drafts, never for ship.

userStories.title: AI cost dashboard with per-workspace quotas
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I want full visibility into AI spend per workspace so I can bill / cap accurately.
acceptanceCriteria: Every adapter call logs to ai_costs: workspace_id, provider, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost_cents, request_id, feature (which feature called it)
Dashboard: cost by workspace, by feature, by model — daily / monthly views
Per-workspace monthly quota; warn at 80%, hard-stop at 100% (overrideable)
Forecasted spend based on rolling 7-day average
Alerts: anomaly detection (sudden 3x spike) → email/Slack
userStories.notes: Anomaly detection catches infinite-loop bugs and rogue jobs before they consume the monthly budget.

userStories.title: Webhook event bus for downstream consumers
userStories.description: As a developer integrating the blog system, I want webhook events for every meaningful state change so I can sync with external systems.
acceptanceCriteria: Events: post.created, post.updated, post.published, post.refreshed, distribution.sent, distribution.failed, brief.approved, refresh_queue.added
Per-workspace webhook config: URL, secret (HMAC signing), event filter, retry policy
Delivery: at-least-once with exponential backoff, dead-letter queue after max attempts
Webhook log viewer: payload, response, timestamp, attempt count
HMAC signature verification documented for consumers
userStories.notes: Always sign webhook payloads — unsigned webhooks are an attack surface.

userStories.title: Public REST API with OpenAPI spec and SDK
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a clean public API so I can build custom workflows and integrations on top of the blog system.
acceptanceCriteria: OpenAPI 3.1 spec auto-generated from route handlers (zod-to-openapi or similar)
Endpoints for every domain object: keywords, briefs, posts, distributions, performance
Auth: API keys per workspace with scoped permissions
Rate limits per API key; documented
Generated TypeScript SDK published to npm; Python SDK as stretch
API docs site (Scalar / Redocly) auto-deployed
userStories.notes: OpenAPI-first means SDKs and docs stay in sync — never hand-write either.

userStories.title: Backup, export, and import per workspace
userStories.description: As a workspace owner, I want full data portability so I can back up, migrate, or comply with deletion requests.
acceptanceCriteria: Export: full workspace data as ZIP (posts as Markdown + frontmatter, assets as files, briefs as Markdown, settings as JSON)
Import: ZIP from another workspace replays into target workspace; collision resolution (skip / overwrite / suffix)
Scheduled backups: daily ZIP to S3-compatible storage per workspace
Retention: 30 days default, configurable
Right-to-delete: full workspace purge job (audit_log preserved with anonymized actor IDs)
userStories.notes: Markdown + frontmatter as the canonical export means consumers can fork to any system without lock-in.

userStories.title: Onboarding checklist and demo workspace seed
userStories.description: As a new workspace owner, I want a guided setup so I'm productive in 30 minutes rather than 3 days.
acceptanceCriteria: Onboarding checklist: connect CMS, set brand voice, connect GA4 + Search Console, connect keyword adapter, connect at least one social platform, write first brief
Demo workspace template: pre-seeded brand voice, sample posts, sample brief — clonable in one click
Tooltips on first-visit per major feature
Progress bar shows % complete; nudges at 1d / 3d / 7d if incomplete
Time-to-first-publish tracked as activation metric
userStories.notes: Time-to-first-publish is the single best activation metric — optimize for it ruthlessly.

userStories.title: Embeddable widget: 'Powered by Blog System' for white-label use
userStories.description: As a host product (Daily OK, etc.), I want to embed the blog admin UI inside my own admin so editors don't context-switch.
acceptanceCriteria: Iframe-able admin UI with postMessage bridge for auth
White-label config: hide 'Blog System' branding, set workspace logo + colors
Single sign-on: parent app issues a signed token; blog system trusts it for the duration
Theming inherits from parent (CSS variables exposed)
Documentation for host app integration
userStories.notes: This is what makes the system reusable across your platforms — without it, every host needs to swap in its own admin.

userStories.title: Compliance: GDPR, CCPA, SOC2-friendly logging
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I want compliance-ready primitives so the system can serve enterprise customers.
acceptanceCriteria: PII inventory: which tables hold PII, what fields, retention policy
Data subject access: export all data for a given user (across workspaces they're a member of)
Right to erasure: anonymize user data while preserving aggregate metrics
Audit log immutability (from US-BLOG-011) and encryption at rest
Data processing addendum (DPA) template
Security overview doc for prospects
userStories.notes: Don't promise SOC2 without an actual audit — but build the foundations now so the audit is cheap later.

userStories.title: End-to-end smoke test: idea → published → distributed → measured
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a single test that exercises the whole pipeline so regressions are caught before they ship.
acceptanceCriteria: E2E test: create workspace → run keyword research → generate brief → generate draft → run QA → publish to test CMS → syndicate to 2 mock platforms → ingest mock metrics
Runs against ephemeral test database + mocked external adapters
Total runtime <5 minutes
CI gate: PRs blocked if E2E fails
Failure mode: each stage screenshots / logs artifact for debugging
userStories.notes: This is the single highest-value test in the system — it catches integration regressions that unit tests miss.

userStories.title: Global agent kill switch + per-action rollback
userStories.description: As a platform admin running the blog system in fully autonomous mode (per scope decision 5D), I need a single "pause all agents" toggle and per-action rollback so any AI-driven publish or re-edit can be halted or reverted in seconds when something goes wrong.
acceptanceCriteria: New blog_agent_settings table per tenant: agents_paused (boolean, default false), paused_at, paused_by_user_id, paused_reason
New endpoint POST /blog/agents/pause and POST /blog/agents/resume (platform admin only) — flips agents_paused atomically

Every agent entry point (auto-refresh, draft pipeline, distribution scheduler, outreach agent, etc.) checks agents_paused at the start of each run; paused state short-circuits with a blog_audit_log entry
Settings page in /platform-admin/blog/settings shows the kill switch as a prominent toggle with last-paused-at + reason

Per-action rollback: every blog_post_revisions row created by an agent is reversible via a "Revert to previous revision" button on the post detail page; revert re-publishes via CMS adapter and writes an audit log entry
Bulk rollback: from the Audit Log page, an admin can select a time range and an agent type and revert every change in that window in one click; confirmation dialog requires typing the tenant name
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Added beyond the original 85-story PRD because scope decision 5D enables fully autonomous re-editing — production-safe autonomy requires a panic button. Treat as a hard gate before US-BLOG-066 ships.

userStories.title: Predictive failure dispatch agent for MFP fleet
userStories.description: As a service manager, I need the platform to predict imminent MFP failures (7-14 days out) from meter trends, error code history, machine age, and last service date so I can dispatch a tech before the customer calls. This flips service from reactive to proactive and is a primary renewal differentiator that competitors (e-automate, Printanista) do not offer.
acceptanceCriteria: New table equipment_failure_predictions in shared/intelligent-alerts-schema.ts: tenant_id, machine_id, predicted_window_start, predicted_window_end, confidence (0-1), signals jsonb, status (pending|approved|dismissed|expired), generated_at

Daily edge function predictive-failure-agent scores every active machine per tenant; signals include meter delta acceleration, error code frequency from existing service ticket history, days since last service, model age, toner cycle anomalies
Predictions above confidence threshold (configurable per tenant, default 0.7) auto-create draft service tickets in pending_review status with linked prediction_id
New page /service/predictions lists predictions sorted by confidence × contract value with signals breakdown, suggested parts, and approve & dispatch / snooze / dismiss actions
Approval creates a dispatched ticket via the existing enhanced-service flow and updates prediction.status
Per-tenant kill switch in settings (mirrors blog kill-switch pattern from US-BLOG-086)
Track precision/recall: tickets closed with same root cause as prediction within 30 days = true positive; expose accuracy stats per machine model
Audit log every approval/dismissal with user + timestamp
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Start with rules-based scoring (interpretable, fast to ship). Move to ML once 6+ months of approval/dismissal feedback exists. Builds on shared/equipment-schema.ts, shared/enhanced-service-schema.ts, shared/intelligent-alerts-schema.ts. Borrow kill-switch pattern from supabase/functions/_shared/safety/kill-switch.ts.

userStories.title: SMS/photo meter reads with vision extraction
userStories.description: As a billing operator, I need customers to text or email a phone photo of the MFP meter panel and have the system auto-extract counters, validate against trend, and create a billable meter read so we eliminate the monthly meter-chasing workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: Twilio inbound SMS webhook routes attached image to edge function meter-read-vision; supports MMS and email-to-SMS gateways
Vision call (Claude Sonnet vision via Anthropic SDK) extracts black total, color total, scan, fax counters as structured JSON
Validation: reject if delta < 0 or > 3x rolling 90-day average; flagged reads land in review queue not auto-billed
Caller phone matched against business_records.phone to identify tenant + customer; ambiguous matches reply asking for site/machine ID
Outbound SMS confirms read or asks for clarification; templates editable per tenant

New table meter_read_submissions: id, tenant_id, source ('sms'|'email'|'web'|'manual'), raw_image_url (Supabase storage), extracted_values jsonb, validation_status, machine_id, submitted_at, reviewed_by_user_id
Admin review UI at /service/meter-reads/review for flagged submissions: side-by-side image + extracted values + edit & approve
Twilio credentials encrypted via existing supabase/functions/_shared/credential-vault.ts (AES-256-GCM)
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Single biggest billing-ops time-saver. Cost-control: cache identical images by hash. Customer texts a number → vision → bill. The 'why didn't we do this sooner' winner. Reuse credential vault pattern; do not roll a new one.

userStories.title: Contract P&L X-ray (live margin per active service contract)
userStories.description: As a dealer owner, I need real-time per-contract margin (CPC revenue minus parts, labor, supplies, financing) so I know which contracts are profitable, which are bleeding, and where to focus renewal negotiation.
acceptanceCriteria: New materialized view contract_pnl_v aggregates: revenue from meter_reads × CPC tier, parts cost from service_tickets.parts_used, labor cost from service_tickets.labor_minutes × tech burdened rate, supplies cost from auto_supply_orders, financing fees from contract terms
Refresh nightly via cron edge function refresh-contract-pnl; on-demand refresh button on the page (rate-limited)
New page /contracts/profitability shows table sortable by margin %: contract, customer, monthly revenue, monthly cost, GP%, 12-month trend sparkline, status badge
Per-contract detail page /contracts/:id/pnl breaks down 12-month cost lines by category with stacked bar chart
Threshold alerts: contracts dropping below 20% GP trigger weekly digest email to OWNER role; threshold configurable per tenant
Filters: location, sales rep, machine model, contract age, customer industry
Export to CSV (margin report) for owner review
Reconciliation check: total contract revenue from view matches GL revenue within 2% over a 30-day window (test fixture)
Permission gated: requires finance.contract.view_pnl permission (new); default-granted to OWNER and PLATFORM_ADMIN
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Most dealers literally don't know which contracts lose money until year-end. Builds on existing shared/contract-renewal-schema.ts, shared/print-cost-calculator-schema.ts, and existing meter_reads + service_tickets tables. Tech: Postgres materialized view, refreshed nightly. Add tenant_id index on the view.

userStories.title: Auto-generated quarterly business review (QBR) decks per customer
userStories.description: As a sales rep covering 50+ accounts, I need overnight-generated QBR decks per customer (usage trends, downtime, savings, upgrade pitch) so I can run quarterly reviews without spending a day per account building slides.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge function qbr-generator runs first Monday of each quarter per tenant, iterating active customers with contracts

Generates per-customer QBR as HTML + PDF with sections: cover, fleet inventory, 4-quarter usage trend (B&W + color volume), downtime/uptime by machine, top 5 service issues, supply cost summary, AI-generated recommendations (consolidation, upgrade, color-shift), next-quarter forecast
Recommendations generated by Claude with structured prompt incorporating fleet snapshot + usage history + service ticket summary; rep can edit before sending
New table qbr_reports: tenant_id, customer_id, quarter (YYYY-Q#), status ('draft'|'reviewed'|'sent'), content_jsonb, pdf_url, generated_at, sent_at, sent_by_user_id
PDF rendered server-side via Playwright (already a project dep) into Supabase storage
UI page /customers/:id/qbrs lists generated QBRs with status pills; 'Review & send' opens editor with rich-text section overrides
Send via existing email infrastructure with branded template; track open + click via UTM
Per-customer suppress flag (some customers don't want QBRs)
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Sales reps love anything that removes deck-building. Reuses Playwright (already in stack for E2E). Recommendations should cite specific data points ('your color volume is up 22% Q-over-Q') to feel real, not generic.

userStories.title: Voice-first field tech ticket close on mobile
userStories.description: As a field tech, I need to close a service ticket by speaking on my phone (actions taken, parts used, labor time) so I do not have to type on a laptop in the van. The system transcribes, extracts structured fields, deducts parts, and drafts the invoice.
acceptanceCriteria: New mobile route /m/service/:ticketId/close-voice with prominent record button (touch target ≥48px per CLAUDE.md mobile-first guidance)
Audio recorded via browser MediaRecorder, uploaded to edge function voice-ticket-close

Transcription via Whisper API (or Deepgram) → Claude extracts structured JSON: actions_taken, parts_used (with SKU resolution), labor_minutes, follow_up_needed (boolean), customer_signature_collected (boolean), customer_satisfaction_note
Unknown SKUs trigger inline disambiguation (top 3 fuzzy matches from inventory) before save
Tech reviews extracted fields, edits inline, confirms close
On confirm: ticket closed, parts deducted from truck inventory, invoice line items drafted (status: pending_approval), labor logged
Offline support: audio queued in IndexedDB if no signal; syncs on reconnect with retry + dedupe
Privacy: audio purged 30 days after ticket close; transcript retained on ticket as 'tech_voice_note'
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Verify on mobile viewport using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Builds on shared/mobile-service-schema.ts. Use OpenAI Whisper (cheaper) for v1; revisit if accuracy on tech jargon is poor. Inventory deduct must be transactional with ticket close.

userStories.title: Tech knowledge graph: RAG over every historical service ticket
userStories.description: As a field tech encountering an unfamiliar error, I need to search 'E-225 on iR-ADV C5560' and get the top historical fixes for that exact symptom on that model so I do not waste time diagnosing a problem we have already solved 50 times. This proprietary data is Printyx's competitive moat.
acceptanceCriteria: pgvector extension enabled on Supabase Postgres
New column embedding vector(1536) on service_tickets (or sidecar table service_ticket_embeddings if migration is risky)
Pipeline: every closed service ticket embedded via OpenAI text-embedding-3-small from concatenated resolution_notes + parts_used + machine_model + error_codes
Backfill job embeds the last 24 months of closed tickets on first deploy; subsequent updates re-embed via DB trigger or webhook

New endpoint POST /api/service/knowledge-search { query, machine_model?, error_code? } returns top 10 ranked tickets with relevance score, summary, parts swapped, mean resolution time, fix-success rate
Mobile-friendly UI: search bar above ticket detail page, results show 'this fix worked X% of the time on this model'
Multi-tenant scoped by default; platform admin can opt tenants into a federated cross-tenant pool with PII redaction (customer name, address, contact removed) — explicit consent required, not default
Permission: requires service.knowledge.search permission; default-granted to all tech roles
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: This is the competitive moat — proprietary failure-and-fix data nobody else has. Federated cross-tenant pool is enormous value but needs careful PII redaction + opt-in. v1 should ship single-tenant; federated pool as v2 once redaction is bulletproof.

userStories.title: Predictive parts truck stocking optimizer
userStories.description: As a service manager, I need the system to recommend optimal parts to stock on each tech's truck based on their territory's fleet composition and 90-day failure patterns so techs do not return to base for parts and we eliminate the 'I had to come back' callback.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge function truck-stock-optimizer runs Sunday nights
Inputs per tech: assigned territories, machines on contract within those territories, last-90-day parts-used distribution by model + part SKU, current truck inventory, part cost + size
Output: recommended truck stock list with quantities, deltas vs current, expected fill rate (% of jobs in next 90 days expected to be completable from truck stock alone)
New table truck_inventory: tenant_id, tech_user_id, part_sku, quantity_on_truck, last_audited_at, capacity_constraint
New page /service/truck-stocking shows per-tech recommendation: 'stock these 8 additional parts to improve fill rate from 78% → 92%' with restock CSV/print
Restock workflow: warehouse staff marks pick list complete; tech confirms received → updates truck_inventory
Track callback root cause when missing-part is the reason; feed into model accuracy stats
Capacity constraint per tech (max parts × volume); optimizer respects it
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Pairs with US-SUPER-001 (predictive failure) — once we know what is failing, we know what parts to load. Validate that parts inventory + service_tickets.parts_used schemas exist before sprint planning.

userStories.title: Deal desk copilot sidebar in quote/order builder
userStories.description: As a sales rep building a quote, I need a context sidebar with account history, similar deals, live margin, and likely objections so I close faster, price correctly, and never get blindsided by an open service ticket on the account I am quoting.
acceptanceCriteria: Right sidebar component <DealDeskCopilot quoteId={...} /> rendered on quote edit page
Account snapshot panel: open service tickets count + severity, AR aging buckets, last 3 quote outcomes (won/lost/expired), churn-risk score (links to US-SUPER-009)
Similar deals panel: top 5 historical closed deals matched on machine class + customer headcount range + region with close rate, avg discount, avg deal size
Live margin panel: quote total revenue vs cost (parts + service-cost-modeling estimate + financing), GP$, GP%, threshold warning if below tenant-configured floor (default 30%)
Likely objections panel: Claude generates 3-5 likely objections with suggested responses based on account history + quote contents + similar-deal patterns
Sub-second initial render: account snapshot from Postgres in <200ms; AI panels stream in

userStories.title: Build authoritative route-parity matrix (frontend ↔ edge ↔ Express ↔ proxy map)

Documents the architecture fact at top: prod frontend → functions.printyx.net via getApiUrl for ALL /api/*; Express proxy map (33 prefixes) only affects dev; Express stays canonical for /api/client-metrics/* (agent) and /install/*
